# Police Community Support Officer (PCSO)

**Make a difference where it matters most**

Join British Transport Police as a Police Community Support Officer and play a vital role in protecting passengers, supporting communities and keeping the railway safe.

**Location:** Cardiff, Newport, Pontypridd and Swansea  
**Salary:** £29,483.96 per year  
**Shift Allowance:** Up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training  
**Annual Leave:**28 days, rising to 30 days with service

**Why become a BTP PCSO?**

Police Community Support Officers are an integral part of British Transport Police.

As a PCSO, you will provide a visible and reassuring presence across the railway network. You will engage with passengers, support railway staff, respond to local concerns and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Chief Superintendent David Rams explains:

*“Our PCSOs are an integral part of British Transport Police. They carry out vital work across the railway network to keep passengers and staff safe, delivering an exceptional service to our communities across England and Wales.”*

**The difference you will make**

As a BTP PCSO, you will help prevent crime, reduce disruption, support vulnerable people and build public trust and confidence across the railway network.

No two days will be the same. You will:

* Conduct visible patrols at stations and across the rail network
* Support victims and provide reassurance to passengers, railway staff and the public
* Assist with minor investigations and intelligence gathering
* Help manage security threats and operational incidents
* Build strong relationships with communities and partner organisations
* Work alongside Police Officers and other policing colleagues
* Help identify and respond to local concerns affecting the railway

**An enhanced operational role**

Unlike PCSOs in many Home Office police forces, BTP PCSOs are trained and equipped with handcuffs. This reflects the distinctive operational environment in which our PCSOs work and the important contribution they make to keeping the railway safe.

**What we are looking for**

We are looking for people who:

* Are resilient and able to remain calm under pressure
* Can communicate confidently with people from different backgrounds
* Demonstrate excellent customer service skills
* Have strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities
* Are committed to supporting communities and building trust
* Can use good judgement when responding to challenging situations
* Work effectively as part of a team
* Share our commitment to providing an excellent service to the public

You do not need previous policing experience to apply. We are interested in your values, motivation, transferable skills and potential to succeed in the role.

**What you will receive**

In return for the important work you undertake, you will receive:

* A salary of £29,483.96 per year
* A shift allowance of up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training
* 28 days’ annual leave, rising to 30 days with service
* Travel benefits
* Ongoing learning and professional development
* Access to in-house talent and development teams
* Career development opportunities across British Transport Police
* A defined contribution pension scheme administered by Royal London

**Develop your career with BTP**

A career as a Police Community Support Officer is rewarding and important in its own right.

PCSOs play a vital role in neighbourhood policing, safeguarding vulnerable people, solving problems within communities and building public trust and confidence across the railway network.

British Transport Police is committed to supporting your long-term development. You will have opportunities to broaden your knowledge, strengthen your operational skills and explore career development opportunities across the organisation.

If you later decide to pursue a career as a Police Constable, successful completion of your PCSO probationary period will also satisfy the work experience requirement for the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP).

This is one of several possible development opportunities available to you and does not diminish the importance or professional standing of the PCSO role.

**Where you could work**

We are recruiting PCSOs in South Wales:

* Cardiff
* Newport
* Pontypridd
* Swansea

**Working patterns**

Policing the railway requires flexibility.

You must be prepared to work shifts, including weekends and bank holidays. Further information about working patterns will be provided during the recruitment process.

**Before you apply**

Please review the following requirements carefully.

You will not be eligible to apply if:

* You have been unsuccessful at interview for a BTP PCSO role within the last three months
* You have been unsuccessful at the application or online testing stage for a PCSO, Police Officer or Special Constable role within the last three months
* You have failed BTP vetting within the last 24 months
* You have received a custodial or suspended sentence
* You have been dismissed from a police force or are currently under investigation
* You have a current County Court Judgment, unmanaged Individual Voluntary Arrangement or unresolved bankruptcy
* You do not have the right to work in the UK
* You have not lived continuously in the UK for the past three years
* You have tattoos that are considered offensive

*Visible tattoos will be assessed individually.*

**Declaring previous matters**

All cautions, convictions and previous police involvement must be declared as part of your application.

Declaring a previous matter does not necessarily mean that your application will be unsuccessful. Each case will be considered individually.

**Your application journey**

**1. Online Application**

Complete and submit the online application form, providing accurate information about your experience, motivation and suitability for the role.

**2. Situational Judgement Test**

As part of the selection process, you will complete an online Situational Judgement Test.

The assessment will consider how you are likely to respond to situations that may arise in the PCSO role.

If you are unsuccessful, you may reapply after three months.

**3. Further Recruitment Stages**

If you successfully complete the initial application and assessment stages, you will receive information about the next stages of the recruitment process.

**4. Candidate P****ool**

Successful applicants will be placed in a 12-month candidate pool and considered for vacancies as they arise.

Placement in the candidate pool does not guarantee an immediate appointment or a posting at a particular location.

*We encourage you to attend a **Recruitment Q&A Session** before applying. The session will help you understand more about the PCSO role, the working environment and the recruitment process.*

**Everyone is welcome at BTP**

British Transport Police is committed to building a workforce where everyone feels that they belong.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and lived experiences. Diversity strengthens our teams and improves our ability to understand and serve passengers, railway staff and communities.

We are committed to providing a fair and accessible recruitment process.

If you require a reasonable adjustment at any stage, please tell us what support you need. We are here to help you participate fully in the recruitment process.

**A note about using AI**

AI tools may help you organise or structure your application, but your answers should reflect your own experiences, motivation and understanding of the role.

We want to hear your authentic voice. You should be prepared to discuss the examples and information included in your application at later stages of the recruitment process.

***Apply now!**The closing date for applications is **midnight** on **24****th October 2026**.*

**Need help?**

If you have questions about the role, your eligibility, reasonable adjustments or the application process, please contact:

**RecruitmentTeam@btp.police.uk**

All enquiries will be treated in confidence.

**Join British Transport Police and help keep the railway safe every da****y**

# Police Community Support Officer (PCSO)

**Make a difference where it matters most**

Join British Transport Police as a Police Community Support Officer and play a vital role in protecting passengers, supporting communities and keeping the railway safe.

**Location:** Bangor and Rhyl  
**Salary:** £29,483.96 per year  
**Shift Allowance:** Up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training  
**Annual Leave:**28 days, rising to 30 days with service

**Why become a BTP PCSO?**

Police Community Support Officers are an integral part of British Transport Police.

As a PCSO, you will provide a visible and reassuring presence across the railway network. You will engage with passengers, support railway staff, respond to local concerns and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Chief Superintendent David Rams explains:

*“Our PCSOs are an integral part of British Transport Police. They carry out vital work across the railway network to keep passengers and staff safe, delivering an exceptional service to our communities across England and Wales.”*

**The difference you will make**

As a BTP PCSO, you will help prevent crime, reduce disruption, support vulnerable people and build public trust and confidence across the railway network.

No two days will be the same. You will:

* Conduct visible patrols at stations and across the rail network
* Support victims and provide reassurance to passengers, railway staff and the public
* Assist with minor investigations and intelligence gathering
* Help manage security threats and operational incidents
* Build strong relationships with communities and partner organisations
* Work alongside Police Officers and other policing colleagues
* Help identify and respond to local concerns affecting the railway

**An enhanced operational role**

Unlike PCSOs in many Home Office police forces, BTP PCSOs are trained and equipped with handcuffs. This reflects the distinctive operational environment in which our PCSOs work and the important contribution they make to keeping the railway safe.

**What we are looking for**

We are looking for people who:

* Are resilient and able to remain calm under pressure
* Can communicate confidently with people from different backgrounds
* Demonstrate excellent customer service skills
* Have strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities
* Are committed to supporting communities and building trust
* Can use good judgement when responding to challenging situations
* Work effectively as part of a team
* Share our commitment to providing an excellent service to the public

You do not need previous policing experience to apply. We are interested in your values, motivation, transferable skills and potential to succeed in the role.

**What you will receive**

In return for the important work you undertake, you will receive:

* A salary of £29,483.96 per year
* A shift allowance of up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training
* 28 days’ annual leave, rising to 30 days with service
* Travel benefits
* Ongoing learning and professional development
* Access to in-house talent and development teams
* Career development opportunities across British Transport Police
* A defined contribution pension scheme administered by Royal London

**Develop your career with BTP**

A career as a Police Community Support Officer is rewarding and important in its own right.

PCSOs play a vital role in neighbourhood policing, safeguarding vulnerable people, solving problems within communities and building public trust and confidence across the railway network.

British Transport Police is committed to supporting your long-term development. You will have opportunities to broaden your knowledge, strengthen your operational skills and explore career development opportunities across the organisation.

If you later decide to pursue a career as a Police Constable, successful completion of your PCSO probationary period will also satisfy the work experience requirement for the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP).

This is one of several possible development opportunities available to you and does not diminish the importance or professional standing of the PCSO role.

**Where you could work**

We are recruiting PCSOs in North Wales:

* Bangor
* Rhyl

**Working patterns**

Policing the railway requires flexibility.

You must be prepared to work shifts, including weekends and bank holidays. Further information about working patterns will be provided during the recruitment process.

**Before you apply**

Please review the following requirements carefully.

You will not be eligible to apply if:

* You have been unsuccessful at interview for a BTP PCSO role within the last three months
* You have been unsuccessful at the application or online testing stage for a PCSO, Police Officer or Special Constable role within the last three months
* You have failed BTP vetting within the last 24 months
* You have received a custodial or suspended sentence
* You have been dismissed from a police force or are currently under investigation
* You have a current County Court Judgment, unmanaged Individual Voluntary Arrangement or unresolved bankruptcy
* You do not have the right to work in the UK
* You have not lived continuously in the UK for the past three years
* You have tattoos that are considered offensive

*Visible tattoos will be assessed individually.*

**Declaring previous matters**

All cautions, convictions and previous police involvement must be declared as part of your application.

Declaring a previous matter does not necessarily mean that your application will be unsuccessful. Each case will be considered individually.

**Your application journey**

**1. Online Application**

Complete and submit the online application form, providing accurate information about your experience, motivation and suitability for the role.

**2. Situational Judgement Test**

As part of the selection process, you will complete an online Situational Judgement Test.

**WHAT WILL YOU BE DOING?**

* Carry out quality control checks during production, including CCP monitoring, label verification, weights and review of shift documentation.

* Verify metal detection and foreign body controls at the required frequency.
* Carry out hygiene and cleaning verification (e.g. ATP swabbing).
* Complete organoleptic assessment of finished product against specification.
* Conduct environmental monitoring and product sampling in line with quality management system requirements, and record results accurately.
* Manage product under positive release, making sure it is held until results are approved and released in line with the release procedure.
* Place product on hold where it does not meet specification or where food safety or quality is at risk, [including stopping production where necessary].
* Make sure all stock on hold or in quarantine is resolved within specified timeframes, in line with the hold and release procedure.
* Keep retained production samples organised, labelled and easy to locate.

**Non-conformances and complaints**

* Raise non-conformances and support manufacturing with investigations, including root cause analysis.
* Support the QA Manager with customer complaint investigations by gathering evidence, identifying likely root causes and following up agreed corrective actions.

**Audits and compliance**

* Carry out internal audits in line with the audit schedule (e.g. glass and brittle plastics, GMP, knife, pen, traceability).
* Support external, customer and certification audits.
* Maintain calibration of Technical equipment in line with the calibration schedule.
* Keep traceability records accurate and up to date, and support traceability exercises.
* Coach production teammates on GMP, hygiene and allergen standards on the shop floor.
* Make sure HACCP, food safety standards and internal quality procedures are followed across manufacturing.

* Identify and suggest improvements to food safety and quality systems and processes within the manufacturing facility.

* Conduct environmental monitoring and product sampling in line with quality management system requirements and ensure results are reported accurately.
* To ensure there is control of product samples under positive release

* Ensure compliance with HACCP, food safety standards and internal quality protocols.

* Level 2 Food Safety and Level 2 HACCP, or equivalent.
* Previous experience in a quality assurance or quality control role within food, supplement or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Working knowledge of GMP and HACCP principles.
* Computer literate, with experience of [Microsoft Office / Google Workspace].

* Strong attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
* Confident in communicating with production teams, including challenging when standards are not met.
* Able to manage multiple tasks, prioritise and meet deadlines

**NICE-TO-HAVES:**

* Level 3 Food Safety and/or Level 3 HACCP.
* Experience working to BRCGS or another GFSI-recognised standard.
* Internal auditor training.
* Experience using root cause analysis tools (e.g. 5 Whys, fishbone).

We are the UK's aviation and aerospace regulator and recognised as a world leader in its field. Our activities are diverse, enabling the aviation industry to meet the highest safety standards, and we pride ourselves on our ability to adapt to the constantly evolving aviation environment.

The restructuring of UK airspace is facilitated through airspace change proposals submitted to the CAA by a range of aviation and non-aviation stakeholders. These proposals vary greatly in terms of size, operational complexity, and scale of consequential impacts, and are required to follow the CAA’s CAP1616 Airspace Change approval process. The Airspace experts within AR perform oversight of such proposals with respect to their impact on existing airspace structures, airports, and all users of airspace, ensuring modern standards for regulatory decision-making are fair, transparent, consistent, and proportionate.

**The Role**

Are you looking for an exciting new opportunity to influence the integration of new technologies such as UAS into UK airspace? The CAA is looking for a highly skilled expert, to join the rapidly expanding Airspace Regulation (AR) team during this exciting time as the UK looks to implement a new Airspace Modernisation Strategy. The strategy aims to create an aviation infrastructure for the future to make quicker, quieter and cleaner journeys whilst enabling new technology and user groups to safely integrate into UK Airspace. 

You should have an in-depth understanding of UK airspace and air traffic operations, with an interest or experience in Uncrewed Air System (UAS) operations or integration. If you have the technical expertise and are excited by the idea of being involved in an opportunity like this, then the CAA wants to hear from you. This role provides the opportunity to be at the forefront of evolving airspace change proposals in the UK within a diverse technical team making key decisions. See your expertise help industry to meet the highest of safety standards in this highly rewarding role. 

**Core Accountabilities**

* Support integrating the demands of diverse airspace users such as UAS, e-VTOL/hybrid aircraft, General Aviation, Military Aviation, Commercial Aviation, Spaceports and Space Launch Operators, all within the framework of the Airspace Modernisation Strategy whilst ensuring that the assessment of airspace impacts have been appropriately considered.

* Perform regulatory oversight of the current airspace system to supporting development of polices to integrate new users such as UAS and Advanced Air Mobility.

* Review and scrutinise airspace proposals from a wide range of sponsors such as operators, innovation companies, airports, the military, spaceports, producing objective and independent assessments of the direct and consequential airspace impacts for each proposed airspace change design.

## Automation Scientist

## About Chemify

Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.

Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.

**Location:** Glasgow, UK (on-site)

**Travel:** Minimal

## The Role

We are seeking an Automation Scientist to sit at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, and testing — translating real chemistry onto our robotic synthesis platform and making sure it works. You will take synthetic routes and turn them into automated protocols, run and validate them on our robotic systems, diagnose issues that span chemistry, hardware, firmware, and software, and feed what you learn back to the engineering teams building the platform.

What sets this role apart is the hybrid: you will need a chemist’s judgement, an engineer’s instinct for how the machines work, and a tester’s rigour — all on a platform where code becomes molecules.

If working across chemistry, engineering, and testing on a real-world robotic platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.

## Key Responsibilities

* Translate synthetic chemistry into automated protocols that run on our robotic platform.
* Run, validate, and troubleshoot syntheses end to end, diagnosing issues across chemistry, hardware, firmware, and software.
* Act as the bridge between the chemistry and engineering teams, turning lab reality into clear, actionable feedback.
* Define and run test protocols and acceptance criteria that prove the platform performs against real chemistry.
* Help characterise and improve platform capability, reliability, and reproducibility.
* Contribute to protocols, documentation, and the standards that make automated chemistry repeatable.

  **About You**

  You are a scientist who likes machines — as comfortable reasoning about a reaction as about the robot running it. You enjoy being the person who works out why something did not behave, whether the cause is chemistry, hardware, or code, and you communicate clearly across disciplines.

  ***We expect you to bring:***
* A degree in chemistry or a related science (PhD or equivalent hands-on experience welcome), with real synthetic / wet-lab experience.
* A strong practical bent and genuine interest in automation, robotics, and how the underlying systems work.

## Mechatronics Engineer

## About Chemify

Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.

Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.

**Location:** Glasgow, UK (on-site)

**Travel:** Minimal

## The Role

We are seeking a Mechatronics Engineer to work across the boundaries of our robotic synthesis platform — where mechanics, electronics, and firmware meet. You will design and integrate the motion and actuation systems that physically carry out chemistry, taking subsystems from concept through prototyping to reliable operation, and making sure the disciplines come together into hardware that just works.

What sets this role apart is the breadth: you will live at the interface of mechanical, electronic, and software design, on a platform where all three combine to turn code into molecules.

If working across mechanics, electronics, and firmware on a real-world robotic platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.

## Key Responsibilities

* Design and integrate mechatronic subsystems — motion, actuation, sensing — across mechanical, electronic, and firmware domains.
* Select and integrate motors, drives, sensors, and actuators, and tune them for real-world performance.
* Prototype, bring up, and test electromechanical systems, debugging across discipline boundaries.
* Partner with mechanical, electronics, firmware, and controls engineers to deliver integrated modules.
* Support characterisation, calibration, and reliability of motion and actuation systems.
* Contribute to design reviews and cross-disciplinary standards.

  **About You**

  You are a systems-minded engineer who is happiest where disciplines overlap. You can reason about a mechanism, the electronics that drive it, and the firmware that controls it, and you enjoy making them work together reliably in the real world.

  ***We expect you to bring:***
* Proven, significant experience in mechatronics, robotics, or electromechanical systems engineering.
* Working knowledge across at least two of: mechanical design, electronics, motion control, and embedded firmware.

## About the role

Our customers are building AI products where a wrong value is not an embarrassment but a harm: a missed allergen, an exercise that aggravates an injury, a drug interaction not flagged. They do not need another vector database. They need to be able to say, with evidence, why a value is what it is.

This role decides what we build next for them. That means talking to those teams, understanding the field that actually has to be right, and turning it into slices an engineer can start on Monday, including the acceptance criteria for what must fail closed and what must be provable from a receipt.

The scarce skill here is saying no. The product surface wants to widen constantly (more input formats, more connectors, more knobs) and most of that should wait until the current slice is honest.

## What you'd do

* Talk to teams building on safety-critical catalogs and turn what you hear into slices an engineer can start on Monday
* Own the pipeline end to end as a product: inputs, contracts, curation, release, the deployed tool and its security settings
* Write the acceptance criteria, including what must fail closed and what must be provable from a receipt
* Say no to work that widens the surface before the current slice is honest
* Keep the public roadmap and the site accurate about what is built versus what is planned

## What we need

* Four or more years in product, at least some of it on a technical or developer-facing product
* You can read an API contract and hold your own in a design discussion with engineers
* You write specs that are specific enough to argue with, including the edge cases
* You have killed or cut a feature you liked, and can explain the call
* Comfortable enough with SQL to answer your own questions about usage

## Nice to have, not required

* Background in data quality, catalog management, search or retrieval
* You have worked with a regulated customer and survived a security review
* You have written developer documentation people actually used

## How we work

* Small team, thin slices, shipped weekly. Nothing sits on a branch for a month.
* Reviews are real. Every feature ships with its tests, and a bug found in review is cheaper than one found by a customer.
* Safety-critical means the boring answer usually wins: fail closed, keep the receipt, don't guess.
* We only claim what ships. That applies to the product, the roadmap and the offer letter.

## How hiring works

1. 1A 30-minute call about something you've built and what was hard about it.
2. 2A working session on a real problem from this codebase. You can drive, or we can pair.
3. 3A conversation about how you make decisions when the evidence is thin.
4. 4References, then an offer. We aim to answer within a week at every stage.

## Apply

Tell us about something you've built and what was hard about it. That says more than a CV, and we read every one. Prefer email? support@cloudcrane.in.

# Research Fellow - Political Process Preferences in Europe (PoPPiE) project

**Full Time Fixed Term for 36 months**

We are delighted to welcome applications for the position of Research Fellow within a new ERC-funded research group on Political Process Preferences in Europe (PoPPiE): Rethinking Conceptual, Ontological and Methodological Foundations (https://poppieproject.com/).

The project aims to develop new ways of understanding how citizens and other political actors think their political institutions should function. Existing surveys like the European Social Survey show extremely strong support for liberal democratic values across Europe, yet people are increasingly voting for far-right parties that reject exactly these values.

To make sense of this conundrum, we need to shift away from researching democratic attitudes as a choice between alternative normative models of democracy, such as representative democracy versus direct democracy. Instead, we require an approach that is psychologically more realistic and more closely approximates the reality of the complex democratic systems we inhabit, which do not correspond to the neat conceptual delineations of democratic theories.

The post holder will take a prominent role in developing the conceptual and methodological innovations to create and operationalise the new approach by designing, conducting and analysing original survey research. This will involve connecting with the projects qualitative work, for instance; focus groups and cognitive interviewing to better understand the nature and content of political process preferences, then using the insights from this work to create survey experiments that will test the new approach. The post-holder will take a role in all stages of this process, from conceptualisation to data collection and analysis, as well as writing up and presenting the findings. As such, there is scope for the post-holder to bring their own skills and interests to influence the direction of the research.

This research position will be based in the Department of Politics and International Relations within the Faculty of Social Sciences, at the University of Southampton, and the work will be carried out under the supervision of Rikki Dean (principal investigator of the project). You will join a vibrant Department with a high concentration of scholars at all career levels researching related themes in the Public Opinion Research Network and the Centre for Behavioural, Experimental and Action Research. The position also comes with its own budget for travel and professional development.

To be successful you will have completed your PhD in a relevant (or equivalent professional qualifications). You will have: a strong background in survey research, with previous experience of survey experiments desirable; a track record of research on the political attitudes of the public and/or other key political actors; a facility for solving conceptual and methodological problems; the ability to plan and organise work independently and as part of a team; the ability to write research presentations and papers for peer-reviewed publication. An interest in combining insights from quantitative and qualitative research is also desirable.

The Research Fellow post is full-time fixed-term with a negotiable start date. Hybrid working is possible for this post.

Fifteen scientists (optical physicists, signal processing specialists, physiologists) turn raw optical interference signals into continuous measurements of cerebral physiology a clinician can act on. What slows them down isn't the science; it's the engineering around it. The last head-to-head comparison of two novel methods took six weeks, and most of that had nothing to do with the methods. You'd design the architecture that fixes this: how data, compute, pipelines and evaluation fit together, and the standards that hold it in place. # Retail Engineer (Deployment Strategist), UK

London, United Kingdom

Full-time

CommerceClarity is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on what you can do and how you work with people.

## What the role is about

Retailers still run too much catalog work through spreadsheets and copy-paste: filling missing attributes, adapting products to each marketplace, and keeping thousands of SKUs accurate. CommerceClarity replaces that manual work with AI agents.

As a Retail Engineer you put those agents to work inside each customer’s operation, from discovery and workflow design to integration and production. Part retail consultant, part engineer, working with our customers across the UK.

This is a high-ownership seat. You own our most strategic accounts end to end and you set the delivery method the rest of the team runs on. We weigh attitude and the combination over years on paper: the sweet spot is three to six years, and the right builder energy beats seniority.

This is one of the first seats we are opening in the UK. You would work out of the London hub on UK accounts, with the platform and the delivery method already built behind you in Milan and Barcelona.

## A job that did not exist three years ago

New tools tend to produce job titles that were not there a few years earlier. Growth engineer and marketing engineer both appeared once the people who understood the funnel could write the code that ran it, and forward deployed engineer and deployment strategist appeared when the same thing happened to enterprise delivery. None of them was a rename. They exist because splitting the person who understands the process from the person who builds it stopped paying for itself.

Retail Engineer is that seat for catalog operations. Outside retail the same job is called deployment strategist, and most of the people who fit it have spent five or six years in solution delivery or solution consulting at a retail software vendor or a consultancy. They read business processes for a living and they own the customer, and almost all of them have a technical side they were never given room to use: the configuration screen ended exactly where the interesting part started, and everything past it went to a development team on another continent.

What changed is the platform. The agents are built there, changed there and run there, so the person who designs the workflow is the person who builds it, in front of the customer, in the same week. You write the prompts and you wire up their systems, and when a number moves you go and change whatever produced it. AI coding assistants work alongside you, so a change that used to take a sprint becomes a prompt and a test.

The half of the job you were already good at stays. Discovery, a room full of stakeholders, an account that trusts you: here that is what keeps the building honest, because you are the one who heard what they actually meant. What you gain is the other half. You spend your days on agent design, evals and prompt engineering, inside a company that runs its own operations on agents, which is a faster education in this than anything you could sign up for.

## Why this role is different

It is not pure delivery and it is not pure engineering. You sit at the intersection: you understand the retailer’s catalog workflow well enough to redesign it around agents, and you have the depth to build the agent flows yourself.

You cover the whole lifecycle. The preparation, mapping their processes, designing the workflow, writing and iterating the prompts, defining the KPIs. Then the run, deployment, integration with their systems, monitoring, debugging, and optimization against those KPIs.

And you do not only deliver. You shape how we deliver and you grow the engineers around you, so one senior hire lifts the team instead of adding a pair of hands. You work closely with the Agent Product Managers, who own the product direction, and with the AI Engineers on delivery.

## What you would do

* Lead agent implementations end to end for enterprise retailers, from kickoff to production, on our DIPE method: design, implement, prove, evolve.
* Own our most strategic accounts and the heaviest proofs of concept directly.
* Define the success KPIs with the customer, and build the measurement loop that proves the agents are working.
* Design and build the agent workflows, and write the prompt layer that drives them.
* Integrate agents with customer systems: PIM, ERP, ecommerce platforms, marketplaces, data warehouses.
* Own the run. Monitor, debug, iterate on prompts and flows, and move the numbers over time.
* Structure how we deliver, and grow the engineers around you, so the team scales on method instead of drowning.
* Feed what you learn back into the product and the agent roadmap.

## What we are looking for

### Essential

* Three or more years of experience, most of it in consulting or solution delivery. Many of our best fits are management engineers who read a business process and enjoy working with data.
* You sit between business and technology. You can redesign a retailer’s catalog workflow and build the agent flow yourself. Not a pure PM, not a pure data engineer.
* Prompt engineering sense. You iterate against real data, you measure output quality, and you know when to fix something with a prompt and when to fix it with code.
* Standing with enterprise customers, and a record of bringing complex delivery home.
* You have managed projects and people, and you still want to build rather than only coordinate.
* Customer-facing and high agency. You handle ambiguity, you lead the conversation with the retailer, and you do not wait for a perfect brief.
* English to native standard, and you are at home in the UK market. Italian is a plus.

### Preferred

* Hands-on with workflow builders such as n8n, and with AI-native coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex.
* Comfortable coding with AI assistance, in Python or TypeScript, to glue systems together and extend what an agent does.
* You have worked with a workflow orchestration engine.
* Deep retail workflow knowledge: catalog management, PIM, assortment, attribute governance, channel publishing, marketplace operations.
* The major PIM platforms, Akeneo, Salsify, inRiver, Pimcore, and the feed and channel managers.
* A background as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Implementation Lead or technical CSM at an enterprise software company.
* Retail data quality at scale: millions of SKUs, many languages, many marketplaces.

## The team you would join

Our founders have spent their careers building and operating retail at scale. They have founded retail companies generating tens of millions in revenue, launched and scaled Amazon’s operations in Italy and Spain, led operations at Everli across more than 2,000 employees, and shaped product direction at Shopify and Zalando. Operator, founder, product leader. Every seat that defined modern European commerce.

## What we offer

* Ownership. Your work reaches production and customers fast, and shapes the delivery method directly.
* Growth. A high-leverage team, real commercial complexity, tight feedback loops.
* An ambitious roadmap. Help define the operating infrastructure for agentic commerce in Europe.
* A new craft. You learn to build and ship with agents and AI coding assistants, and it compounds.
* Flexible hybrid. The London hub, three days a week minimum, plus four remote weeks a year.

Condé Nast is one of the world's most renowned media publishing companies, creating and distributing every type of media today, spanning print and digital publishing in all formats. With a portfolio of some of today's most influential brands, the company continues to grow its audience through a global operational and content infrastructure across its 12 owned and operated markets. Headquartered in New York City, the company's owned and operated markets include China, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico & Latin America, Spain, Taiwan, UAE/Dubai, the U.K., and the U.S., with additional local license partners in over twenty additional markets across the globe. Lead brands include Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ, Architectural Digest, Condé Nast Traveler, Vanity Fair, Wired, Allure, Ars Technica, Bon Appétit, House & Garden, Pitchfork, Tatler, and Vogue Business.

# **Job Description**

Location:

London, GB

**Condé Nast thrives on collaboration, and our teams come together in the office four days a week (Monday - Thursday).**

We value diversity of background, views and cultures. We celebrate people for their personal qualities, skills and contributions, recognising the power our brands have to influence and shape culture.

  

The New Yorker brings a distinctive editorial voice to everything it creates. Our goal is to build a stronger, more habitual relationship with our readers, making reading and play a valued part of their everyday lives. Across The New Yorker’s digital experiences and our Puzzles & Games offering, you’ll help give people compelling reasons to return: something worth reading, listening to or watching, a satisfying game, and thoughtful connections between visits.

  

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to help shape these experiences across web and apps. Your work will span games themselves and the experiences around them, from gameplay and feedback to discovery, onboarding and the journeys that bring readers and players back. You’ll combine strong visual and interaction craft with clear product thinking, taking a key role in progressing initiatives from early exploration through launch and iteration. You’ll work closely with design leads, product managers, engineers, researchers and editorial partners to turn open questions into considered, usable products.

  

We’re also evolving how we design and build. You’ll bring curiosity and familiarity with AI tools, with room to develop your skills in prototyping and working more directly with code as part of the role.

  

## What you'll be doing

  

Connecting reading and play to lasting habits You design both games and the experiences around them, exploring and refining gameplay alongside discovery, onboarding, progress and returning to play. You connect this work to the wider reader experience, considering how each interaction builds familiarity, enjoyment and reasons to return. You question assumptions and work with your partners to define what is worth solving and how you’ll know it has worked.

  

Bringing editorial character to digital experiences You translate distinctive brand identities into clear, engaging interfaces. You bring care to typography, hierarchy, layout and interaction, balancing the character of the brand with usability, accessibility and the needs of different devices.

  

Making interaction feel right You use prototypes to explore behaviour, timing, motion and feedback. Whether you’re refining a reading journey, helping someone discover a game or developing an interaction within one, you pay attention to the details that make an experience intuitive and satisfying.

  

Understanding readers and players You seek out research, analytics and direct feedback to inform your decisions. You run lightweight usability testing, partnering with UX Research where deeper investigation is needed, and use what you learn to improve the work.

  

Designing with and contributing to systems You use shared components, patterns and design tokens confidently, recognising where consistency helps and where a new approach is justified. You contribute reusable solutions that support brand expression and work within the realities of our platforms.

  

Staying close to implementation You collaborate with engineers throughout the design process, discussing feasibility early and reviewing the experience as it is built. You work through interaction details, edge cases and visual QA so the quality of the shipped product reflects the intent of the design.

  

Using AI as part of your practice You explore where AI tools can add value to your design practice, building on your experience and learning alongside the team. You experiment with ways to develop ideas, prototype and collaborate with engineering, applying your judgement to the results and sharing what you learn.

  

Learning from what ships You agree intended outcomes with your product and engineering partners, then use analytics and qualitative feedback to understand performance. You connect design decisions to measures such as engagement, repeat use and retention, and identify where further iteration will make a difference.

  

Contributing to the team You communicate your thinking clearly, build productive relationships across disciplines and participate actively in critique. You share your work and methods, support other designers and bring an open, constructive approach to feedback.

  

## You'll thrive in this role if...

  

* You bring strong visual and interaction design skills, with particular care for typography, detail and the quality of the finished experience.
* You can take an ambiguous problem and turn it into a clear direction, working with others to make sensible decisions about scope and priorities.
* You’re interested in editorial products, puzzles and games, and what makes people return to an experience over time.

**Every structure starts below the surface — and getting that right takes skill, curiosity, and a deep understanding of the ground itself. We’re seeking motivated Graduate Engineers ready to take on those challenges from the start. Do you thrive on solving complex, real-world engineering problems? Do you want to contribute to some of the UK's most complex and prestigious projects? Then join our team and let's get to work.**

**Create Solutions that will enable a better tomorrow**

We are growing our Ground Engineering team across the UK and looking for a Graduate Engineer to be part of it. You will contribute to some of the UK’s most prestigious and complex infrastructure programmes while working alongside experienced engineers who will guide your path to Chartership through a tailored development plan.

Typically you will be:

* Carrying out a broad range of geotechnical engineering design activities, from collating and interpreting ground investigation data, running geotechnical analyses and numerical models, to preparing calculations and technical reports that meet project requirements and the highest quality standards
* Undertaking engineering geological mapping and ground modelling at site scale, producing desk study reports, ground investigation reports, geotechnical design reports, and ground investigation specifications
* Supporting and supervising ground investigations on site, gaining experience across a variety of ground conditions and project types
* Checking calculations and technical drawings from other engineers, expanding your technical judgment and ability to notice details
* Applying and promoting engineering best practice across the team, including use of in-house tools such as our carbon calculation tool, supporting our commitment to sustainable and responsible design
* Planning and prioritising your workload with support from your project manager, tracking and reporting progress against project budget and programme
* Handling your own deliverables responsibly while ensuring accuracy and quality by thoroughly checking your work
* Attending site visits or client meetings

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.**

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners, or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

 On top of this you will have:

* A bachelor's or master's degree in either Civil/Structural/Geotechnical Engineering (BEng, BSc, Meng, MSc), or Geology together with an MSc in either Engineering Geology or Geotechnical Engineering, either completed or due to be awarded this summer
* A genuine motivation to become a Chartered Engineer or Chartered Geologist, with the resolve and persistence to get there
* Some practical experience in an engineering environment, whether through a year in industry, summer placements, or a final year project or dissertation with real-world geotechnical, geological or engineering geology application
* Interest in and enthusiasm for engineering geology and geotechnical engineering, together with curiosity about subsurface behaviour
* The ability to work and collaborate effectively within diverse, multi-disciplinary project teams
* Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present technical findings clearly and professionally to colleagues and clients
* Commitment to quality, precision and technical excellence

**A place to work and so much more**

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers. We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home. With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

**What we also offer:**  
To us, a fair reward is more than a competitive salary. We want to take care of our people professionally and personally as well.  
Some of our benefits include:

* 28 days' holiday plus all UK bank and public holidays
* Formalised development plans and yearly promotion opportunities
* Private health care, for you and a contribution from you for your immediate dependents
* Flexible and hybrid working conditions
* Annual subscription fees paid for your membership of two Professional Institutions
* Group personal pension scheme – salary exchange
* Life assurance
* Maternity Leave: 1-20 weeks full pay, 21-26 weeks half pay, 27-39 Statutory (SMP) 40-52 weeks unpaid (eligibility criteria will apply)

Optional benefits include:

**Got more questions?**

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Shruti Gupta at srgu@cowi.com.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

# Lead Data Engineer

Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom

**Working at CreateFuture**  
  
CreateFuture is an **AI-native consulting partner**where people do work that matters and are supported to do it well. We work alongside organisations such as PayPal, adidas, NatWest, FanDuel and Money Saving Expert, building digital products and services that make a difference  while always putting people first.

We’re a team of creators. We write code, shape delivery, build go-to-market strategies, develop AI solutions and create the practices that support our people. We work side by side with our clients, challenging what’s not working and helping them to build the future. Our commitment to craft, quality, and culture has helped us scale to over 600 people in just a few years.  
  
CreateFuture is a Great Place to Work-CertifiedTM company and has won Best Workplaces UK multiple years in a row.

**Join us on our journey. Let’s create tomorrow, together, today.**

### **About the role and team:**

We are looking for a Lead Data Engineer to own the technical direction of a data engagement, working with Microsoft Fabric, Python, and PySpark across our data team. You'll lead a team of data engineers, setting the standards for how pipelines and architecture are designed, built, and operated, while remaining hands-on with the most complex technical challenges. You'll work closely with client stakeholders and CreateFuture's wider engineering capability to ensure delivery is both technically excellent and commercially sound.

### **What you'll be doing:**

* Own the technical direction of a data engagement, setting standards for pipeline architecture, data modelling, testing, and operational readiness
* Lead and technically direct a team of data engineers, allocating work, reviewing designs and code, and unblocking technical challenges
* Design and evolve data platform architecture on Microsoft Fabric, including data pipelines, Azure OneLake, and the broader Azure ecosystem
* Set and enforce CI/CD, testing, and operational practices across the engagement's data engineering workflows, using Azure DevOps
* Build professional relationships with key client stakeholders, translating business and data requirements into a coherent technical roadmap
* Troubleshoot and resolve the most complex issues in live data pipelines, and lead incident response when things go wrong

### **We'd love to talk to you if you:**

* + Have extensive hands-on experience with a modern cloud data platform such as Microsoft Fabric (our current client's platform), Databricks, Snowflake, or Synapse, including designing production data platforms — the platform is the wrapper, not the skill, and strong engineering depth on one transfers readily to another
  + Have deep SQL expertise and a strong grasp of data modelling and architecture (Kimball, data vault, medallion/lakehouse patterns, or domain modelling) — this is the clearest line between someone who operates a platform and someone who can design on top of it, and it's provider-agnostic
  + Have strong proficiency in Python and PySpark for batch/ELT data processing at scale (this role centres on batch pipeline engineering — we treat streaming/real-time as a separate discipline and never assume the two are interchangeable)
  + Have led or technically directed a team of data engineers, setting standards for pipeline design, testing, and delivery
  + Have experience owning CI/CD and operational practices for data engineering workflows, ideally using Azure DevOps
  + Are experienced working directly with client stakeholders, building trust and challenging where appropriate
  + Have familiarity with the broader Azure ecosystem, including Azure OneLake and Azure ML, particularly for model industrialisation

### **What we’ll offer you:**

We trust people to do their best work. That means flexibility over rigid rules, impact over activity, and real investment in your growth both professionally and personally. You’ll be part of a supportive, and friendly culture, surrounded by smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do.  
  
We offer flexible working, including hybrid and remote options. Our office hubs are located in Edinburgh, Leeds, Manchester, London and Bulgaria, with occasional travel to client sites or CreateFuture offices when needed.

We trust you to manage your time balancing collaboration with client time and focused work. What matters is the impact you have, not how busy you look.

### **Our hiring process**

We try to keep our hiring process clear, fair and respectful of your time. We aim to get back to everyone who applies and we will be upfront about where you are in the process.

It usually looks like this:

* Call with our Talent Acquisition Team
* Role specific capability interview

Depending on the role, we might also ask you to do a short presentation, a practical or technical task or have a values focused conversation. We will explain what is involved before anything happens.

### **Inclusion at CreateFuture**

We believe diverse teams build better workplaces and better products. We want CreateFuture to be a place where people feel able to be themselves and do their best work.

If you need any adjustments or support during the application process, just. We will do what we can to help.

We look forward to your application!

## The opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity to be a key part of the LCC Media School’s student-centred employability offer in the 2026-27 academic year.

We are looking for a part-time (0.5) fixed term Coordinator for our Diploma in Professional Studies (DPS), which is our optional industry experience year positioned between the second and third year of our undergraduate courses. During the year students undertake a variety of activities to improve their employability in their chosen field, including placements and work-based learning projects.

This role will work alongside the existing DPS Coordinator (0.5) on a fixed term basis until 31 July 2027 to oversee the DPS course provision for the Media School. Your responsibilities will include course management, the monitoring and assessment of student progress, managing a team of industry mentors, and developing and maintaining relationships with a network of employers in the media and creative industries who can provide placement and collaborative work-based learning opportunities to our students.

You will work predominantly onsite at our Elephant and Castle campus for two and a half days a week, with the potential for hybrid working where appropriate.

## Your profile

This is a role for someone who can integrate the needs of students, employers and the University in providing work-based learning opportunities for undergraduate students to support their employability.

You will bring experience of academic leadership, teaching, assessment and quality enhancement, alongside a strong understanding of trends and issues in UK Higher Education relating to student outcomes and employability.

You will have experience working with students and employers on work-based learning opportunities at scale and be a persuasive, inclusive, and thoughtful communicator, able to work confidently with students, colleagues, external partners, and wider professional communities.

You will have knowledge and experience of the media and creative industries, particularly in relation to the School’s portfolio of courses in media, communications, journalism, publishing and photography.

As a coordinator of resources, you will have experience motivating teams and communities of practice, setting direction across functions, promoting collaboration across boundaries, managing budgets effectively, and managing complex projects, competing priorities, and demands, while always remaining focused on student outcomes and experience.

If you have any queries about this role or need any reasonable adjustments for your application, please contact Lesley Wilkins, Senior Resourcing Adviser, lcc.staffrecruit@arts.ac.uk

## We are UAL

University of the Arts London (UAL) generates and inspires the creativity the world needs for a better future. Since 1842, our colleges have been defining creative education. With curiosity, imagination and intent we make work which creates lasting change for people and our planet. London is core to who we are, a place where we meet and share ideas with people from different backgrounds and cultures.

Our creative network influences learning, culture, industry and society on a global scale. Our academics and practitioners deliver creative education and inspire new ways of thinking through research and innovation. We work with students at every level from pre-degree and short courses to postgraduate and online learning, enabling them to build the careers they want. Together, we are a community of makers, thinkers, pioneers and storytellers redesigning the future.

As a University, we are ranked second in the world for Art and Design. We are formed of 6 Colleges with unique histories and identities: Camberwell College of Arts, Central Saint Martins, Chelsea College of Arts, London College of Communication, London College of Fashion and Wimbledon College of Arts. UAL also has 4 Institutes, 5 Research Centres, 1 Pre-Degree School and 2 subsidiary companies delivering specialist activities.

We are a global University, welcoming over 22,000 students and 6,000 staff from 130 countries. We aim to be a university where people can be themselves and feel supported to reach their full potential. That’s why we are proud to hold a Bronze Award from the Race Equality Charter (REC), are members of the Business Disability Forum and Employers for Carers, and maintain our status as a Disability Confident Scheme and Living Wage employer.

## Application process

We operate a fair and open anonymous selection process. Thus, you will need to create an account and submit an application through our job board. As part of this, you will need to provide a supporting statement/answer some competency questions to demonstrate your suitability. Our recruitment process involves: Application, Shortlisting, Interview and Assessment, Offer, Onboarding.

We understand the benefits of using AI in work. But, if you are thinking of using it to submit an application, we ask you to think about what value it adds. AI tools tend to lack the personal touch and authenticity we value in candidates. We encourage you to showcase your unique knowledge and skills using your own voice.

If we receive a high volume of applications, the closing day date might close early. We aim to communicate any changes to the closing date with at least 24 hours’ notice. If you have any general questions or have accessibility needs, please refer to our Contact us page.

Please read through our FAQs before applying and Recruitment Process before applying.

The Deputy Head of Stage supports the delivery of world-class productions, exhibitions, concerts and events across Factory International.

Working closely with the Head of Stage, you will lead stage operations, venue changeovers, technical installations and staffing resources, ensuring the highest standards of safety, efficiency and artistic excellence.

You will provide day-to-day leadership to technical teams, collaborate with artists and visiting companies, and play a key role in the successful delivery of diverse and ambitious projects.

## Deputy Head of Stage Responsibilities

* Support the Head of Department in the deployment and operation of all aspects of Factory International's technical stage equipment within the Scenic & Gallery Installations team, with particular emphasis on stage operations, show running and venue changeovers.
* Responsibility for deputising for the Head of Stage during periods of absence.
* Support the Head of Department with staffing levels, rota management and resource planning, ensuring appropriate staffing levels are maintained across all projects and activities.
* Support Exhibition Installation team members as required to ensure exhibitions, installations and productions are delivered to the highest artistic, technical and operational standards.
* Participate in the planning, organisation and supervision of get-ins, fit-ups, technical rehearsals, performances, show runs and get-outs. Ensure appropriate staffing and equipment resources are allocated and utilised in accordance with current Health & Safety legislation and environmental best practice.
* Lead discipline-specific team members in the creation and delivery of artworks, exhibitions, concerts, performances and events. Plan and supervise venue format changeovers, including stage installations, de-rigs, seating reconfigurations and exhibition installations.
* Coordinate truck and vehicle movements on site and operate the venue truck lift system in accordance with established procedures and safety requirements.
* Attend production meetings, rehearsals and technical rehearsals as required. Liaise with visiting productions, artists, technical teams and contractors to ensure their requirements are met and that all activities are compliant with Factory International policies and procedures.
* Work collaboratively with Production Management, Technical Departments, Building Operations and Artistic teams to ensure seamless delivery of all projects and events.
* Support the development of production-related income streams and contribute to maximising commercial opportunities for the organisation.
* Cover the position of Technical Duty Manager on a rota basis and oversee other technical departments in the absence of the relevant manager.
* Support the Rigging Department and other technical departments as operational requirements dictate.
* Assist in the planning and delivery of departmental budgets, resource allocation and equipment procurement, ensuring value for money and operational effectiveness.
* Coordinate and supervise external contractors, suppliers and specialist technicians, ensuring compliance with Factory International standards and safety procedures.
* In conjunction with other technical team members, plan and deliver an effective programme of maintenance, including Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM), housekeeping, stock control, inspection and testing of equipment and venue infrastructure.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of departmental systems, procedures and working practices to enhance efficiency, safety and service delivery.
* In conjunction with the Head of Department, Technical Manager and Director of Production & Building Operations, support the recruitment, training, development and succession planning of technical staff.
* Promote positive working practices within the department and provide effective leadership, supervision and mentoring to permanent, freelance and casual staff.
* Act as a key point of contact during operational incidents and emergency situations, ensuring procedures are followed and appropriate actions are taken.
* Champion sustainable working practices and support Factory International's environmental commitments through efficient use of resources, waste reduction and responsible working methods.

## Deputy Head of Stage Person Specification

### ESSENTIAL

* Extensive practical knowledge and proven experience of event staging and operations within one or more art forms (live music, theatre, exhibitions, performance art or related disciplines), preferably within a producing or receiving venue.
* Demonstrable experience of leading and delivering large-scale productions, exhibitions, events or installations.
* Working knowledge of technical stage management, rigging practices and venue operations.
* Proven experience of supervising and developing staff, with strong leadership and people management skills.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships at all levels.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, solve problems effectively and work under pressure in a fast-paced environment.
* Experience of receiving and/or delivering large-scale national and international touring productions.
* Experience of workforce planning, scheduling and rota management.
* Experience working with artists, visiting companies, contractors and multidisciplinary teams.
* Knowledge of technical drawing software including AutoCAD, Vectorworks or equivalent.
* Knowledge of the principles relating to the safe deployment and use of electrical systems within an entertainment environment.
* Strong understanding of Health & Safety legislation, risk assessment processes and safe systems of work.
* Comfortable working at height and within complex technical environments.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant resource and scheduling systems.
* Commitment to championing representation and inclusion at every level of the organisation with a proven ability to work with people from a wide range of backgrounds

### DESIRABLE

* Practical knowledge of LOLER, PUWER and other relevant Health & Safety regulations applicable to performance venues and exhibition environments.
* IPAF, MEWP and PASMA certification.
* Experience managing gallery installations, exhibitions, public art projects or artist commissions.
* Good understanding of statutory regulations governing venues, including the Working Time Regulations.
* Experience using Artifax Event, Vectorworks, AutoCAD or similar venue management and planning software.
* Awareness of current and emerging trends in venue technologies, automation systems and event production practices.
* Experience touring nationally and/or internationally.
* Experience acting as Technical Duty Manager, Event Manager or equivalent operational leadership role.
* Experience of budget management, project planning and resource allocation.
* Full UK Driving Licence.
* Technical theatre qualification from an accredited college, university, ABTT or equivalent industry-recognised training.
* Vocational qualifications such as IRATA, PASMA, IPAF, CITB or equivalent.
* Current First Aid at Work qualification.
* Understanding of ABTT Technical Standards for Places of Entertainment.
* Enthusiasm for training, mentoring and support of emerging talent

The University of Birmingham is proud to have been a part of the City of Birmingham and the wider region for over 100 years, and we are equally proud to be recognised as a leading global university. We want to attract talented people from across the city and beyond, support them to succeed, and celebrate their success.

We are committed to helping the people who work here to develop through our sector-leading Birmingham Professional programme which provides all professional services staff with development opportunities and the encouragement to reach their full potential. We believe there is no such thing as a typical member of staff and that diversity is a source of strength that underpins the exchange of ideas, innovation, and debate. We are a place of open, critical thinking, and the creation, sharing and dissemination of knowledge. Professional Services put students at the heart of all they do and enable an exceptional educational experience. ## Job description

**Who we are** :

Delta Capita is a global managed services, consulting and technology solutions provider, combining deep Financial Services expertise with technology innovation capabilities.

Our mission is to reinvent the financial services value chain through technology-enabled, mutualised services that help financial institutions transform, optimise and grow.

**Role Summary :**

Delta Capita's Consulting business is growing rapidly, and we are looking for an experienced Financial Services consulting salesperson to drive new client acquisition across the UK market.

This is a true new business development role focused on winning net-new logos across banking, financial institutions, challenger banks, building societies and fintechs.

You will be responsible for opening relationships with prospective clients and converting them into long-term consulting customers across our core practices:

* Change & Transformation
* Risk & Regulation
* Data, Technology & AI

This is an individual contributor role reporting directly to the Head of Consulting. You will have direct access to Delta Capita's leadership team, consulting practice leaders and subject matter experts, supporting you throughout the sales cycle.

Once a client is won, delivery and account leadership teams will take responsibility for ongoing growth and delivery, allowing you to remain focused on developing new opportunities and expanding the client base.

The role is based in London with a hybrid working model and regular client-facing engagement.

## Job requirements

**Key Responsibilities :**

1. Build and execute a target account strategy across the UK banking and financial services market, including retail banks, corporate banks, investment banks, building societies, challenger banks, neo-banks and fintechs.
2. Generate and manage your own pipeline through networking, referrals, outbound prospecting, industry events and strategic partnerships.
3. Secure meetings with senior decision makers including CEOs, COOs, CIOs, CTOs, CROs, Heads of Change, Heads of Regulatory Change and Heads of Data.
4. Lead opportunities from initial engagement through proposal, RFP, commercial negotiation and contract execution.
5. Develop and maintain a £3m-£4m qualified pipeline of new client opportunities.
6. Deliver accurate forecasting, reporting and opportunity management through Salesforce.
7. Collaborate closely with Consulting leadership, subject matter experts and Marketing to drive targeted campaigns and business development initiatives.
8. Represent Delta Capita at industry events and client engagements.

**How Success Will Be Measured (Year One) :**

1. Win 3 new client logos.
2. Deliver £1m in new-client bookings.
3. Build and maintain a qualified pipeline of £3m-£4m.
4. Achieve a minimum of 5 senior-level first meetings per month with target prospects.

 

**Required Experience :**

1. Proven success in winning new logos by selling consulting, professional services or transformation solutions into Financial Services organisations.
2. Strong track record of selling consulting services into banks, financial institutions, challenger banks or fintechs.
3. Demonstrable experience managing the full sales lifecycle, including:

   * Opportunity qualification
   * Proposal development
   * RFP responses
   * Commercial negotiations
   * Contract execution
4. Experience managing multiple complex sales cycles simultaneously.
5. Strong pipeline generation capability with experience building opportunities from the ground up.
6. Knowledge of key sales disciplines and tools including Salesforce, forecasting methodologies and partner-led sales.
7. Strong understanding of the UK Financial Services market, competitive landscape and buying behaviours.

**Required Skills :**

## About The Role

**Role Title:** Women’s Professional Development Phase Coach  
**Department:** Women’s Football
