# Purpose of the Role

To lead the delivery of the full-time Women’s Professional Development Phase programme based at York College, creating a high-performance learning environment that integrates football development with players’ education. The postholder will support the technical, tactical, physical, psychological and social development of players, planning, delivering and reviewing coaching and match programmes aligned to the programme’s playing philosophy and performance objectives. Working closely with York College and multidisciplinary colleagues, the coach will maximise each player’s progression through individual development planning and prepare players for senior women’s football.

# Key Responsibilities

* Lead the planning, delivery and review of the coaching programme for players in the Women’s Professional Development Phase.
* Deliver high-quality training sessions and matchday coaching in line with the programme’s game model, coaching methodology and player development priorities.
* Lead the PDP games programme on Wednesdays and take responsibility for either the U18s JPL team on Saturdays or the York City Women’s B team on Sundays, including match preparation, team selection, matchday delivery and post-match review.
* Plan the football programme around the York College timetable, working collaboratively with college staff to support players’ educational progress, attendance and wellbeing.
* Create and maintain Individual Development Plans for players, ensuring targets are clear, measurable and regularly reviewed.
* Monitor player progress through observation, review meetings, performance feedback, video and relevant performance data.
* Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary staff, including sports science, medical, education, and safeguarding colleagues, to provide a genuinely holistic development programme.
* Support players joining and progressing through the programme, contributing to succession planning and transition into senior women’s football, further education or other appropriate pathways.
* Contribute to squad management, player selection, match planning and post-match review processes.
* Maintain accurate and timely programme records, including session plans, player reviews, development updates and required performance or education monitoring systems.
* Attend and contribute to programme meetings, player reviews, continuing professional development and wider football and college discussions.
* Work closely with staff across the women’s pathway to ensure continuity of coaching and effective transition between development stages.
* Contribute to the identification, recruitment and assessment of prospective players and trialists when required.
* Act as a positive role model, maintaining high professional standards and reinforcing the values and behaviours expected within the programme and York College environment.

# Key Relationships

The postholder will work closely with the Head of Education Partnerships, Women’s Head Coach, Designated Safeguarding Officer and York College teaching and support staff, multidisciplinary practitioners, education colleagues, and coaches across the wider women’s pathway. The role will also involve regular communication with players, parents/carers, senior-team staff and external partners where appropriate.

# Safeguarding, Compliance and Professional Standards

* Promote and uphold the highest standards of safeguarding, player welfare and student wellbeing at all times.
* Comply with all club, York College, competition and governing body policies and procedures, including safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion, health and safety, anti-discrimination, confidentiality and data protection.
* Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and behaviours expected when working with young people.
* Ensure all coaching practice is safe, age-appropriate and reflective of current best practice in women’s player development.
* Undertake mandatory training and maintain all qualifications, licences and clearances required for the role.

This job description is intended to outline the main duties and responsibilities of the role. It is not exhaustive, and the postholder may be required to undertake other duties appropriate to the level and nature of the position.

## About The Candidate

## Essential

* UEFA B Licence or equivalent coaching qualification appropriate to the level of the role.
* Experience of coaching within a high-performance youth, academy, college or women’s football environment, ideally within the Professional Development Phase.
* Strong understanding of player development within the women’s pathway, including individual learning, transition and progression planning.
* Ability to design and deliver high-quality training and match programmes for players in the Professional Development Phase.
* Experience of creating, monitoring and reviewing Individual Development Plans and player feedback processes.
* Ability to work effectively with college staff and within a multidisciplinary team, building strong professional relationships.
* Excellent communication, organisation and planning skills, with the ability to coordinate football and education commitments.
* A clear commitment to safeguarding, welfare and the holistic development of young people.
* FA safeguarding and first aid qualifications, or willingness to obtain and maintain them.
* Enhanced DBS clearance and eligibility to work in the UK.

## Desirable

* FA Advanced Youth Award or equivalent youth development qualification.
* Uefa A License
* Experience of working in the women’s and girls’ game, particularly with full-time college-based players or players transitioning towards senior football.
* Experience of supporting dual football and education programmes.
* Experience of using video, data and performance management systems to support player development.
* Knowledge of competition, player registration and performance planning requirements relevant to the women’s game.
* Full UK driving licence.

* Player-centred and development focused.
* High standards of professionalism, integrity and accountability.
* Collaborative and respectful in working with colleagues, college staff and stakeholders.
* Reflective, organised and committed to continuous improvement.
* Resilient, adaptable and able to perform effectively in a fast-paced football and education environment.

* Manage voyage orders, pro-forma invoices, documentary instructions, vessel nominations, Letters of Credit, Provisional and Final cargo insurance, Narrowing/Nomination of dates/quantities, Vessel clearance, etc.

* An understanding of trading and shipping operations activities (e.g. cargo, time charters, voyage charters, ships, quality and quantity controls).

* Strong motivation, dedication and results-oriented approach to work.
* High attention to detail, organised, structured and logical.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships both internally and externally.
* Able to work at fast-pace in a dynamic trading environment with time-sensitive, business critical activities requiring 24/7 responsiveness.

* A positive attitude and a proactive, results-oriented approach, with strong organisational skills.

We’re Failbetter Games, an award-winning game development studio and makers of *Sunless Sea*, *Sunless Skies*, *Mandrake* and *Fallen London*. We’re known for inventive narrative design, atmospheric storytelling, and rich, fantastical settings.

We’re looking for a Writer and Narrative Designer to join our small in-house team at either a senior or mid level, working specifically on *Fallen London*. This position is permanent, remote, and full time, which for us means 35 hours a week.

We’re based in the United Kingdom, but as long as you can be available during our core hours of 11:00 to 16:00 UK time, you don’t have to be.

Also, if you are based elsewhere, it’s likely we’ll have to structure this as a contract position: we’ve found the administrative requirements for direct employment can be impractical for a studio our size in many jurisdictions.

**About the Role**

You’ll be working on *Fallen London*, an unusual narrative browser game about life in a version of Victorian London that was stolen and installed in a vast underground cavern.

The game is over 16 years old, with more than four and a half million words last time we counted. It’s a live-service RPG we’re actively updating, and very politely free-to-play: development is funded mostly by monthly subscriptions and premium stories. A tabletop roleplaying game in the setting raised over a million dollars on Kickstarter in 2025.

Because we’re a small team, your duties will be varied. You can expect to do all of the following:

* Pitch story arcs to other writers, and take part in high-level planning for the next several months of work.
* Write stories of varying length, complexity, and tone, with a wider range of subject matter than video games usually explore.
* Design quality-based narrative structures that support story and theme while also giving rise to enjoyable gameplay.
* Update and extend existing content (for example, for seasonal events).
* Offer feedback on work by other writers.
* Provide short pieces of marketing copy to explain released or upcoming stories to players – the equivalent of a book’s blurb.
* Draft briefs for artists to help them illustrate your work.

**Requirements**

You don’t need a particular degree or some arbitrary number of shipped titles or years’ experience to work for us. As long as you’re able to do the job well and can demonstrate that in your application, we’d love to hear from you.

Because *Fallen London* is primarily a narrative game and more oriented towards prose than dialogue, we find it benefits from conventional writing skills, of the kind that would be helpful for writing a novel or short story.

Our writing is also denser in choice and consequence than is usual in video games. We use an approach we call quality-based narrative. Qualities, in our parlance, might represent any of the following (and other things besides):

* A character’s capabilities which we can test when the player attempts challenges – for example, how persuasive they are, or their skill with Shapeling Arts.
* Complications and menaces. These might track how scandalised polite society is by a character’s behaviour, or mounting peril on an underground ocean.
* Currencies and resources. These might be physical, like souls in bottles, or abstract, like terrible secrets.
* Aspects of world state that reflect the progress of their current activities, like a complex theft or archaeological expedition.

We're interested in the ways interactivity can produce literary effects, akin to how a writer of conventional fiction might use devices like foreshadowing, metaphor, or just careful choice of syntax or diction.  One example we're known for is choices that tempt the player to go against their own character's interests for the sake of humour, emotional catharsis, or plain curiosity.

For this role, we don’t require you to have done previous work with quality-based narrative, but you will need to be comfortable translating your story ideas into this framework. We anticipate that this will usually require you to have experience with some form of interactive writing that goes beyond branching narrative.

Finally, although you don’t need to be a native speaker of English, you will need a very high level of proficiency, including a sensitivity to the nuances of words.

**Optional Extras**

Any of the following would be helpful and worth telling us about in your application, but they’re very much secondary and not required for you to apply:

* Familiarity with *Fallen London* or other games in the same setting.
* System design skills, such as balancing costs and rewards or defining progression curves. (All of *Fallen London*’s game mechanics are also narrative mechanics, so these skills are useful to our writing team.)
* Experience writing functional specs or otherwise clearly explaining desired tooling or game features to programmers.
* Experience guiding freelance writers, from pitching through to completion of a story. (This won’t be part of your initial responsibilities, but many of our monthly Exceptional Stories are written by freelancers, so it could be helpful once you settle into the role.)

**Remote Work**

The entire team is remote, and you don’t have to live in the UK.  That said, we’re a British company and pay UK salaries; whether that works in your favour will depend on your location. In particular, this means that our positions are usually not a good fit for residents of the United States, where industry salaries and general cost of living both tend to be much higher.

As mentioned above, we will need you to be available between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC/BST – the way we work benefits too much from real-time communication for us to work asynchronously.  How well these hours work for you will usually depend on your own time zone, which accordingly we’ll ask you to tell us as part of the application.

Based on our experience of earlier vacancies, we’d advise that you think carefully before applying if you’re four or more hours removed from the UK. And if you’re six or more hours removed, we’d recommend not applying at all unless there’s something highly unusual about your personal circumstances.

We’re open to sponsoring a UK work visa for this role. If that’s your preference, you are of course welcome to apply regardless of current time zone.

**What We Can Offer**

Failbetter is committed to offering employees a safe, respectful environment, a healthy work-life balance, and transparent decision-making. We strive to avoid crunch and enthusiastically eliminate systemic sources of overtime. We don’t talk over one another in meetings, and we don’t expect all our employees to share the same hobbies and cultural references.

We’ve received a GamesIndustry.biz Best Places to Work award four years out of the last seven, and received their Diversity Award in 2022.

Further benefits of working here include:

* Flexible start times, and strong support for other forms of flexible working, like compressed hours.
* Twenty-five days of leave in addition to UK public holidays.
* Additional leave in every fifth year, as a long service bonus.
* Excellent provisions for parental leave.
* Employer pension contributions.
* Private health insurance.
* Private dental care.
* Reimbursement for annual Covid and flu vaccines.
* Opportunities for paid attendance at industry events.
* An annual, expenses-paid trip to a scenic part of the UK, for our company gathering.
* One silent day a week, to work free of meetings or Slack interruptions.
* Periodic consultations in which we invite subject matter experts to teach us about topics relevant to our work.

If you’re outside the UK and we offer you a contract position, we won’t be able to provide all of these, but we’ll pay you at a higher rate to compensate.

**How to Apply**

If you’d like to be considered for the role, you can apply by completing this single-page form before 9:00 BST on  21 October 2026. The form has nine questions. Most are basic things like name and country of residence. Aside from that, the main things we ask for are:

* A PDF version of your CV.
* One to three short writing samples, at least one must be either prose fiction or from a game (for more details, see the application form and the additional topics section below).
* A cover letter.

**What to Expect After Applying**

You should hear from us within two weeks of the deadline; often, we’re able to reply considerably sooner. We’ll let you know whether or not you make it to the next stage of applications.

We generally invite 5-15% of candidates to that second stage, which involves answering a few short written questions. The third and final stage is a remote interview that usually lasts between 60 and 90 minutes.

#### Additional Topics

**Will you provide feedback on my application?**

If someone completes the second stage of our hiring process, we’re generally able to provide feedback.

Unfortunately, it isn't feasible for us to do so on first-stage applications – we get too many, relative to the size of our team. Also, a lot of the time we'd just be repeating standard advice that's widely available online.

**How long should my writing samples be?**

The length is up to you. However, the shorter the sample, the more likely it is that we'll read the parts that best demonstrate your abilities. It might be better to send us an excerpt with a paragraph of two of context, rather than a full 12 000 word chapter.

**What kinds of samples would be most useful? Are there any you don’t recommend?**

The most useful samples for *Fallen London* tend to be prose fiction, or anything that shows how you’ve used interactivity in your writing.  For this reason, we require that at least one sample be prose fiction or from a game.

We generally find it hard to draw useful conclusions from screenplays.  Please don’t send us more than one of these.

We won’t generally look at non-fiction samples, as it’s too hard to draw conclusions from them about your preparedness for the role.  There are probably some very niche exceptions (if, for example, you made a piece of interactive non-fiction that does something playful or interesting with the player’s input).

**Can I use fan fiction as a sample?**

Yes – we have no prejudices against it. That said, we’d ask that you not send us *Fallen London* fan fiction – paradoxically, that makes certain things harder to judge.

**Should I write a sample tailored specifically to this application?**

We’d advise against it. At this initial stage, we’re looking for general information about your skills as a writer and narrative designer. You don’t need to send us something that matches *Fallen London*’s style, demonstrates detailed knowledge of Victorian England, or otherwise hews particularly close to our existing work.

That said, there probably are situations where it might make sense to write something new – for example, if you’re having trouble picking samples because everything that represents your current abilities is under NDA.  But if so, we’d still recommend writing something you expect to be of wider benefit to your portfolio, rather than for this single vacancy.

# Customer Experience Business Analyst - Fix Term Contract 1 Year

* Full-time

## Company Description

Fastmarkets is an industry-leading price-reporting agency (PRA) and information provider for global commodities, providing price data, news, analytics and events for the agriculture, forest products, metals and mining and new-generation energy markets.

Fastmarkets' data is critical for customers seeking to understand and predict dynamic, sometimes opaque markets, enabling trading and risk management. Fastmarkets is a global business with a history dating back to 1865 and is built on trust and deep market knowledge. It has more than 700 employees spread across global locations in the UK, US, China, India, Singapore, Brazil, Belgium, Bulgaria, Finland and beyond.

## Job Description

**The Role**

The Business Analyst will work closely with the product, business and technology teams to identify and resolve gaps in requirements to address business problems and customer needs. The role will combine strong business analysis practice with practical use of artificial intelligence to improve the speed, quality and consistency of discovery, requirements definition, process design and delivery.

This role will help the business lean further into AI-driven ways of working. It will identify where AI, automation and better use of data can remove low-value manual activity, improve decision-making and create better customer and colleague experiences. The Business Analyst will test opportunities responsibly, show measurable value and help teams adopt new approaches while maintaining appropriate human oversight, information security and data quality.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working with complex systems, including pricing and data platforms, and moving between process mapping, user journeys, data analysis, user stories, acceptance criteria and lightweight prototypes. They will use AI as a co-pilot, not a substitute for judgement, stakeholder engagement or accountability.

**Principal Accountabilities**

* Own requirements from discovery through delivery, ensuring clear, complete and agreed outcomes.
* Lead stakeholder engagement to gather requirements, challenge assumptions and uncover business needs.
* Translate business objectives into high-quality user stories, acceptance criteria and process flows.
* Own backlog quality and readiness, ensuring priorities are clearly defined and delivery-ready.
* Manage analysis activities independently across multiple initiatives with minimal supervision.
* Facilitate workshops and discovery sessions to align business, customer and technical requirements.
* Analyse and improve business processes to drive efficiency, scalability and customer value.
* Define success measures, support testing and validate outcomes against business objectives.
* Identify and resolve requirements risks, dependencies, gaps and ambiguities early in delivery.
* Use AI tools as part of daily analysis activities to improve research, documentation, backlog refinement and decision-making.
* Identify, test and champion practical uses of AI and automation that help teams work smarter while maintaining appropriate governance and oversight.

## Qualifications

We recruit talented, dynamic people with diverse backgrounds and experiences, all united by a belief in our mission to provide the world’s leading and most trusted price reporting, events, and intelligence service for the markets we serve. We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a fully inclusive workplace, where everyone feels able to participate and contribute meaningfully.

If you are open-minded, curious, resilient, solutions-oriented and committed to promoting equality, then read on.

**KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**

We are looking for an individual who is highly motivated, driven, and have a passion to be part of a fast-paced, successful team. Being a strong team player is also important as well as someone who is happy to work flexibly.

* Strong business analysis skills across discovery, requirements, process mapping, user stories, acceptance criteria and UAT.
* Experience using AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, documentation and automation while validating outputs.
* Ability to redesign processes using automation and AI where it adds value.
* Understanding of prompt design, output evaluation and iterative testing.
* Knowledge of responsible AI principles, including privacy, security and governance.
* Ability to translate data and AI opportunities into clear business and technical requirements.
* Experience creating prototypes and using evidence to inform delivery decisions.
* Experience working with Product Owners and Agile delivery teams.
* Proficient in Jira, Confluence and similar delivery tools.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.
* Strong facilitation, stakeholder management and influencing skills.
* Commercially minded with a focus on customer and business outcomes.
* Experience with complex data, pricing, information services or B2B products desirable.
* Experience with automation, analytics, low-code platforms or AI-enabled products desirable.

If you're excited about the role but your experience, skills or qualifications don't perfectly align, we encourage you to apply anyway.

## Additional Information

**Our Values**

Fastmarkets people come from all different walks of life. It’s this mix of brilliant personalities, experiences and insights that gives us that warm, open, and friendly culture you can feel as soon as you meet us. But however wonderfully different we all are, there are six things we all have in common – and they form our Fastmarkets values.

Created by our own employees to reflect some of the personal traits that Fastmarkets people have, our values are key to what makes our culture unique. They reflect who each of us are and they're embedded in everything we do. Our values are:

* **METRICS DRIVEN.** We use insights to improve our customers’ experience and our business performance
* **ACCOUNTABLE.** We are accountable to ourselves and those we work with: we keep our promises and get things done
* **GROWTH MINDSET**. This value enables us to be nimble to the changing realities and operate with a sense of urgency
* **INCLUSIVE.** We are inclusive and respectful, celebrating each of us and giving everyone a deep sense of belonging with the desire to bring their best self to work every day.
* **CUSTOMER CENTRIC.** We are customer-centric in all that we do
* **COLLABORATIVE.** We are collaborative, able to work across teams and capitalise on the diversity of intellect, perspectives, and experiences.

We are committed to ensuring all candidates feel welcomed and supported. Should your application advance and you require accommodations for the interview process, please inform us so we can make the necessary arrangements.

**Reward and benefits at Fastmarkets**

We believe in fair pay and benefits that support you both inside and outside of work. Through Fastmarkets Rewards, you'll have access to a range of core benefits and a flexible allowance, giving you the freedom to tailor your package to suit your lifestyle, wellbeing and financial priorities. We know that everyone's needs are different, so we've designed our benefits to support our diverse global team wherever they're based.

*Specific benefits may vary by country and role.*

The postholder is expected to examine processes critically and raise concerns transparently, regardless of seniority or cost, as part of upholding the core principle of data and business integrity.

**Your main responsibilities will be:**

**Deputy and Resilience Function**

* Act as deputy to the PDRC Manager.
* Provide resilience and business continuity across the wider PDRC function.
* Lead the team during periods of absence, leave and increased workload.
* Provide succession capability for the PDRC Manager role.
* Support development of future capability within the function, key departmental objectives and performance initiatives, particularly where progress is at risk from absence or resource constraints elsewhere in the function.

**Commercial Performance and Claims**

* Lead on commercial recovery activity and performance-related claims in the PDRC Manager's absence and support delivery of these areas at all other times.
* Assist in the preparation and review of commercial claims and supporting evidence.
* At times of deputising and where demand requires, represent the function in commercial discussions with TfL and Network Rail.
* Identify opportunities to maximise commercial recovery and minimise liabilities.
* Review commercial claim submissions and appeals.

**Data Assurance and Performance Integrity**

* Lead assurance activities to improve quality and integrity of performance data.
* Validate reporting outputs and ensure information is robust and auditable.
* Challenge data quality issues and implement corrective actions.
* Provide independent assurance of attribution, cancellations and reporting processes and have a working understanding of the delay attribution as a rules-based framework – escalating data quality risks where they're identified.
* Develop processes and controls to improve confidence in business information.

**Performance Insight and Improvement**

* Identify and support performance improvement initiatives through analysis and investigation.
* Support forecasting, scenario planning and business case development activities.
* Identify recurring issues, trends and opportunities.
* Support implementation of recommendations from reviews and investigations.

**Governance and Stakeholder Management**

* Undertake coordination of tracking actions, risks and issues arising from commercial reviews and performance meetings through to resolution.
* Situational awareness of day-to-day operational activity, anticipating likely stakeholder questions, data gaps or emerging issues before they surface, rather than waiting to be asked.
* Continuously examine performance, reporting and commercial processes critically, taking nothing at face value regardless of seniority or experience, and raise concerns transparently.
* Develop relationships with Network Rail, TfL and industry partners, and actively create opportunities for team members to engage with stakeholders directly – through meetings or site visits – building representation and awareness capability across the function, shaping and arranging information to meet their specific needs.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Identify opportunities to improve systems, reporting and efficiency.
* Support automation and process improvement initiatives.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement.
* Support development and application of new tools and reporting products, feeding back on existing tools to improve their effectiveness and identifying new ways they can be applied to improve ways of working within the team.

**As a minimum, you will need to have:**

* Experience within railway performance, commercial, reporting or operational environments, with a specific understanding of train operating principles - how services are timetabled, pathed and operated in practice – sufficient to interpret delay attribution and evidence it correctly.
* Working knowledge of delay attribution and Schedule 7 / Schedule 8 regimes, sufficient to provide credible independent assurance and escalation in this area.
* Experience compiling clear, legible reports, presentations and business cases.
* Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
* Proven forensic approach to evidence – builds conclusions strictly from what can be documented and sourced, drilling into detail and cross referencing until facts are clearly demonstrated.
* A sharp eye for detail others may overlook – you spot inconsistencies, anomalies or gaps in data and reporting that aren't otherwise flagged.
* Sustains accuracy and rigour in repetitive, detail–heavy and time-critical work, with the situational judgement to direct support and resources where they are needed most.
* Has an intrinsic grasp of delay attribution as a rules-based framework – able to separate causation from formal responsibility.
* Experience in handling complex data and information, with excellent organisational and governance skills.
* Demonstrates genuine interest in team members‘ wellbeing and success in their roles, evidenced through specific examples.
* Demonstrates the ability to raise what may appear to be unfavourable findings even at a commercial or reputational cost.
* A demonstrated willingness to question and, where necessary, challenge conclusions or decisions made by more senior or more experienced colleagues based on one's own independent judgement.
* A forward thinker, consistently ahead of the commercial and information curve.
* Corrects their own thinking or conclusions when the evidence requires it, even when doing so doesn't help their own argument.

**Desirable:**

* Experience of performance reporting within a TOC or Network Rail environment.
* Experience in data assurance or governance roles.
* Proactive, ideas – driven approach to continuous improvement, with a track record of advocating and embracing process change.
* Ability to build or adapt automation and reporting tools independently.

Redman Place, Stratford - travel across the full London Overground network required on an adhoc basis

# Non-Executive Director and Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee

## Description

**About GB Group plc**

GB Group plc (“GBG”) is listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 250.

GBG serves customers across the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific through two highly complementary core capabilities of identity and location. Together, these enable organisations to accurately verify identities, prevent fraud and better understand customers, driving the vast majority of our revenues across diverse, regulated and data rich markets.

We deliver our capabilities through a scalable, technology-led platform that supports local market requirements while benefiting from global expertise. Our commercial model is largely based on subscription and consumption contracts, reflecting how embedded our solutions are in our customers’ critical workflows.

This underpins our strong levels of repeatable revenue, stable margins and high cash generation, enabling us to continue investing in product innovation and go-to-market activities globally.

### The Requirement

GBG is led by an experienced Board chaired by Richard Longdon and, as a FTSE 250 company, operates within a more mature governance and reporting framework. The Board is supported by an Audit & Risk Committee with a central role in overseeing financial reporting, internal controls, risk management, external audit and the wider control environment.

The Company is seeking to appoint a high-calibre independent Non-Executive Director who can provide strong financial, governance and risk oversight and chair the Audit & Risk Committee. The successful candidate will bring credibility with investors and other stakeholders and be comfortable operating in a UK listed company environment.

The appointment calls for an individual with recent and relevant financial experience, sound judgement, independence of mind and the ability to support and challenge management constructively in a complex, international, data-led technology business.

The role will require the usual commitment expected of a non-executive director of a FTSE 250 company, including attendance at scheduled Board and Committee meetings and sufficient availability outside formal meetings to support the Chair, executive leadership team and key governance processes. The board typically meets ten times a year, split between the company’s headquarters in Chester and London (one board meeting may be held internationally). The anticipated time commitment is approximately 20 days per year, and the role is paid a base salary of £63,549 with an additional fee for Audit & Risk Committee Chair of £20,000 pa.

### The Successful Candidate

Candidates will have the integrity, independence, sound judgement and personal credibility required of an independent non-executive director of a UK Main Market listed company, together with the stature to chair the Audit & Risk Committee effectively.

In addition to the required ‘recent and relevant’ financial experience, the successful candidate is likely to bring broad international experience from a technology, software, data, digital, payments or other regulated services environment. They will understand the governance, reporting and control expectations of a FTSE 250 business and be capable of adding value in a complex, international, data-led organisation.

The appointee will be expected to contribute meaningfully to Board discussions on strategy, performance, capital allocation, financial reporting, risk management, internal control and assurance. They should be well placed to support the Board and executive team as the Company continues to strengthen its control environment and reporting in line with Main Market expectations, including the evolving requirements of the UK Corporate Governance Code.

They will have strong interpersonal skills, the confidence to engage effectively with Board and management colleagues, and the ability to challenge constructively while maintaining supportive and collaborative relationships. The right candidate will be commercially minded, strategically astute and capable of contributing as a rounded business leader and Board director, in addition to bringing the technical credibility required of an Audit & Risk Committee Chair.

# Principal Data Engineer (we have office locations in Cambridge, Leeds and London)

London, England

Apply now

## Company Description

Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.

Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.

We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.

Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.

We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime - from birth to old age.

## Job Description

**Principal Data Engineer**

At Genomics England, we’re looking for an experienced Principal Data Engineer to help shape the future of data engineering across our organisation.

Our data supports clinical and research use at national scale. Behind this sits a complex engineering challenge: creating secure, resilient and scalable platforms that enable highly sensitive genomic and health data to be used responsibly and effectively.

**This is where you will make a difference**

As Principal Data Engineer, you’ll provide senior technical leadership across our data engineering capability. You’ll help us make thoughtful, sustainable technology choices, establish effective data engineering practices and build robust platforms that teams can confidently develop and operate.

This is a Principal individual contributor role with meaningful scope to influence how data engineering develops across Genomics England. Working across teams and technical domains, you’ll shape direction, provide architectural guidance and remain closely involved in hands-on engineering and delivery.

You’ll collaborate with data engineers, architects, bioinformaticians, product teams, governance colleagues and senior stakeholders to solve complex data engineering challenges across our clinical and research data platforms.

You’ll also lead the development of our wider data engineering capability, helping to shape how we grow and strengthen data engineering practices across the organisation. Through mentoring, technical guidance and knowledge sharing, you’ll support colleagues to grow their expertise and help teams adopt consistent, sustainable approaches to data engineering.

**Why this role matters**

The data platforms behind our clinical and research work need to be secure, reliable and designed for the long term. As Principal Data Engineer, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how we approach those challenges across the organisation.

You’ll influence data engineering beyond a single team while remaining close to the technology and contributing directly to delivery. Your impact will be seen not only in the platforms and solutions you help create, but in the engineering practices you establish, the decisions you help shape and the colleagues you support to develop.

Ultimately, your work will help us build sustainable data engineering capability and enable the responsible use of complex clinical, genomic and research data.

**What you’ll be doing**

* Providing technical leadership across our data engineering capability, helping shape strategic and technical direction, roadmaps and sustainable technology choices

* Setting clear standards, patterns and practices for secure, scalable and reliable data platforms, pipelines and data products

* Leading and contributing hands-on to the design and delivery of complex data solutions across cloud and hybrid environments

* Providing architectural guidance across areas such as Lakehouse, distributed and event-driven systems

* Working collaboratively across engineering, architecture, bioinformatics, product and governance to solve complex technical challenges

* Promoting interoperability, open standards, data modelling, metadata and provenance, supporting the responsible and effective use of data

* Embedding privacy, security and regulatory requirements into platforms handling sensitive clinical and research data

* Strengthening engineering practices and platform resilience through DataOps, DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automation, observability and security by design

* Evaluating emerging technologies and helping teams make thoughtful, appropriate and sustainable technology choices

* Mentoring experienced engineers, sharing knowledge and contributing to technical communities and design groups to help develop capability across the organisation

**What we’re looking for**

You’ll bring substantial data engineering experience and the technical depth to operate at Principal level. Just as importantly, you’ll be comfortable working across teams and organisational boundaries, bringing people together around technical decisions and communicating effectively with stakeholders at different levels.

**What you’ll bring**

* Proven ability to operate at Principal level within data engineering, combining deep technical expertise with experience shaping technical and architectural direction across multiple teams
* The ability to communicate complex technical decisions and trade-offs clearly, build trusted relationships and work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders across a matrix environment
* Extensive experience designing and delivering complex, enterprise-scale data platforms and systems, from initial design through to production

* Deep knowledge of modern data engineering, cloud infrastructure and scalable data storage and processing, alongside strong hands-on programming experience.

* Strong knowledge of data modelling and the wider data lifecycle, including metadata, provenance, governance and approaches to interoperability

* Experience designing secure and resilient systems for sensitive or highly governed data, ideally within a complex, regulated environment such as healthcare, genomics or research

* A strong understanding of modern software engineering practices, including CI/CD, automation, infrastructure as code and platform reliability, with experience establishing reusable patterns and sustainable engineering approaches

* A collaborative approach to technical leadership, with experience mentoring engineers, sharing knowledge and supporting the development of others

* A Master’s degree, or equivalent experience, with a specialism in data or infrastructure

You do not need to come from a genomics background. Experience working with complex, sensitive data in a highly governed environment will be important in this role.

**It would be helpful, but not essential, if you have experience with**

* Genomic, bioinformatics or clinical data platforms, including formats such as VCF, BAM or FASTQ

* Standards such as GA4GH, OMOP or FHIR

* Orchestration technologies such as Airflow, Prefect or AWS Glue

* Lakehouse or data mesh approaches, and batch, streaming, distributed or event-driven architectures

* Secure Data Environments, federated research platforms or clinical systems

* Additional programming languages such as Scala, Java or Shell/Bash

## Qualifications

* A Master’s degree, or equivalent experience, with a specialism in data or infrastructure

## Additional Information

**Salary From:** £103,500  
**Closing Date:** Monday 12th October @ 23:00 (UK time)  
  
Being an integral part of such a meaningful mission is extremely rewarding in itself, but in order to support our people, we’re continually improving our benefits package. We pride ourselves on investing in our people and supporting them to achieve their career goals, as well as offering a benefits package including:

* **Generous Leave:**  **30** days’ holiday, plus bank holidays, plus additional leave for long service, and also the option to apply for up to 30 days of remote working abroad annually (approval required).
* **Family-Friendly:** Blended working arrangements, flexible working, enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave benefits.
* **Pension & Financial:** Defined contribution pension (Genomics England double-matches up to 10%, however you can contribute more if you wish), Life Assurance (3x salary), an Electric Vehicle salary sacrifice scheme and a Give As You Earn scheme.
* **Learning & Development:** Individual learning budgets, support for training and certifications, and reimbursement for one annual professional subscription (approval required).
* **Recognition & Rewards:** Employee recognition programme and referral scheme.
* **Health & Wellbeing:** Subsidised gym membership, a free Headspace account, and access to an Employee Assistance Programme, eye tests, flu jabs.

**Equal opportunities and our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace**

Genomics England is actively committed to providing and supporting an inclusive environment that promotes equity, diversity and inclusion best practice both within our community and in any other area where we have influence. We are proud of our diverse community where everyone can come to work and feel welcomed and treated with respect regardless of any disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, or social background.

Genomics England’s policies of non-discrimination and equity and will be applied fairly to all people, regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, being pregnant or recently becoming a parent, race, religion or beliefs, sex or sexual orientation, length of service, whether full or part-time or employed under a permanent or a fixed-term contract or any other relevant factor.

Genomics England does not tolerate any form of discrimination, harassment, victimisation or bullying at work. Such behaviour undermines our mission and core values and diminishes the dignity, respect and integrity of all parties. Our People policies outline our commitment to inclusivity.

We aim to remove barriers in our recruitment processes and to be flexible with our interview processes. Should you require any adjustments that may help you to fully participate in the recruitment process, we encourage you to discuss this with us.

We have four key behaviours that represent what we would like Genomics England to feel like and the culture we want to encourage, in order for us to achieve our mission. These behaviours help us all work well together, deliver on our outcomes, celebrate our successes and share feedback with each other. You can read about these and other aspects of our culture here Culture | Genomics England

**Blended working model**

Genomics England operates a blended working model as we know our people appreciate the flexibility that hybrid working can bring. We expect most people to come into the office a minimum of 2 times each month. However, this will vary according to role and will be agreed with your team leader. There is no expectation that people will return to the office full time unless they want to, however, some of our roles require full time on site attendance e.g., lab teams, reception team.

Our teams and squads have, and will continue to reflect on what works best for them to work together successfully and have the freedom to design working patterns to suit, beyond the minimum. Our office locations are: Canary Wharf, Cambridge and Leeds.

**Onboarding background checks**

As part of our recruitment process, all successful candidates are subject to a Standard Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check.  We therefore require applicants to disclose any previous offences at point of application, as some unspent convictions may mean we are unable to proceed with your application due to the nature of our work in healthcare.

The team plays an important role in ensuring feedback is responded to appropriately, within relevant statutory and corporate timescales, and that learning from complaints is used to improve services for residents.

As a Customer Feedback Officer, you will lead on customer contact, supporting people through the complaints process by telephone, email, letter and, where required, face to face. You will need to communicate clearly and sensitively with customers who may be upset or experiencing difficult circumstances, while helping to resolve issues at the earliest appropriate stage and keeping people informed throughout.

This is a varied and rewarding role requiring excellent communication skills, attention to detail and the ability to work flexibly across changing priorities. You will be supported by the Complaints Team Managers and will contribute to a service that helps the council listen, respond and improve through the feedback it receives.

**About you:**

We are looking for someone who is confident engaging with customers and colleagues, including in situations that may be complex, sensitive or challenging. You will be able to communicate clearly, listen carefully and respond professionally, helping people to feel informed and supported throughout the complaints process.

You will be organised, flexible and able to manage a range of changing priorities while working to deadlines. In Internal Audit, we ensure that Goldman Sachs maintains effective controls by independently evaluating the firm’s controls, governance, and risk management framework.

As the third line of defense, Internal Audit’s mission is to independently assess the firm’s internal control structure, including the firm’s governance processes and controls and monitor the implementation of management’s control measures. In doing so, internal Audit:

•             Assesses the firm’s control culture and conduct risks

Goldman Sachs Internal Audit comprises individuals from diverse backgrounds including chartered accountants, developers, risk management professionals, cybersecurity professionals, and data scientists. # Engineering Manager - Grafana Application Security | EMEA | (Remote, UK)

United Kingdom (Remote)

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

*This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain, and Ireland.*

**About the role:**

We are looking for an engineering manager to lead our application security engineering team.  You will be responsible for developing and implementing security strategies, as well as liaising with other teams delivering parts of our overall security posture. You'll be accountable for the security of software you don't write, in teams that don't report to you. The people who do well in this role get there by making the secure path the easiest one.

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of implementing and improving the maturity of security programs, through the use of automation and systematic approaches in Cloud-based SaaS organizations, and possess excellent leadership and communication skills.  You can tell the difference between a finding and a risk, and know how to prioritise risk mitigation, guiding the squad towards the most effective use of their time.

You must have significant engineering acumen as this is a highly technology-driven role.  Your main role will be to support your engineering team and to do that you should be able to review a threat model, challenge a severity rating, and contribute to a design review.

**Responsibilities**:

* Lead our application security team covering a range of areas, including application security, cloud security, and internal tooling development.
* Lead 1st and 3rd party vulnerability management, including coordinated disclosure with external reporters and embargoed fixes.
* Define, optimize, and implement the engineering strategy in concert with the security leadership team, ICs and stakeholders across the business.
* Regular 1:1s, coaching and mentoring to ensure your team members are motivated, happy and engaged. Providing continuous feedback to ensure that they can add value while maintaining high standards.
* Collaborating with our engineering leaders and other organization stakeholders to help define and influence wider product strategy, roadmaps and designs.
* Be actively engaged with significant incidents, including preparation, simulation, response, and affected customer notification and communications.
* Contributing to and reviewing design documents for upcoming projects. Ensuring projects are well-defined and ready for development. Advise on how to break down projects into tasks.

**Requirements**:

* Prior experience running a security engineering team.
* You have a strong engineering background and are capable of engaging in technical conversations and challenging teams to arrive at strong technical decisions themselves.
* You will be comfortable working with engineering teams who have a strong sense of autonomy in their decision-making, be it technical or product-focused.
* While you’re great with people and adept at managing relationships, you still keep up-to-date with the latest technical trends and shifts to maintain and enhance your understanding of the challenges your teams face.
* You approach security with a DevOps mindset. You prefer security by enablement, automation, and guardrails over gates and roadblocks.
* You have familiarity with securing and operating on public Cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) providers, with Kubernetes, and with securing combined open-source software (OSS) and SaaS products.
* You are an excellent written and verbal communicator. You can articulate complex cybersecurity concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. You are adept at translating security problems to business impact.

**Bonus Points:**

* A technical background, ideally with programming or software engineering experience, before transitioning into security & leadership.
* Working knowledge of Grafana Labs OSS projects and products. Experience in using observability tooling to solve security problems.
* Experience working with OSS communities.
* Experience securing large-scale distributed systems.

**Compensation & Rewards:**

In the UK, the Base compensation range for this role is £103,958 - £124,750. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

Our brand is recognised and respected in the industries that we serve.

We have a visible and displayed commitment to the industries we serve and the associations and institutions who exist to further these causes. loyee retention are central to our company ethos. We aim to provide a positive, supportive working environment where everyone’s contribution is valued.

As part of our strategic growth we are seeking to recruit a “hands on” experienced and knowledgable Senior Design Engineer who can lead our mechanical design function. Reporting directly to the Technical Director, the Senior Design Engineer will play a leading role within our engineering design function, delivering bespoke shell and tube heat exchanger projects for global customers from concept through to manufacture.

This is a senior-level technical position with responsibility for complex mechanical design work, technical governance, and supporting the development of other engineers within the team. The successful candidate will lead by example, combining strong engineering judgement with the ability to guide, mentor and support colleagues.

The role involves detailed mechanical design of shell and tube heat exchangers, including preparation of engineering drawings and performance of mechanical design calculations.

In addition to hands-on design work, the Senior Design Engineer will contribute to strengthening engineering capability within the business, supporting the development of less experienced engineers and helping maintain consistent application of design codes and best practice.

* Produce and review engineering drawings using Autodesk Inventor
* Perform and validate engineering calculations using PV Elite
* Provide technical input from enquiry stage through to manufacture and delivery
* Review engineering outputs including drawings, calculations and technical documentation
* Work closely with manufacturing, supply chain, customers and inspection bodies
* Support continuous improvement in engineering methods, tools and processes
* Mentor and support junior and developing engineers within the team

* Experience leading engineering teams and managing design activities.
* Thorough understanding of pressure equipment design, materials selection and manufacturing processes.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to work collaboratively across engineering, production and commercial functions.

* Chartered Engineer status or working towards achieving the same
* Experience within the process, petrochemical, energy, chemical or related industries.

We set high standards for our people, and we reward that commitment with competitive pay, development opportunities, and long-term career progression.

**Business Purpose & Value Contribution**

**Key Outcomes Expected**

* ISO 27001 certification and SOC 2 Type II attestation achieved through one efficient control programme
* An external trust centre live, with customer security questionnaires answered to an agreed SLA from a maintained and increasingly automated knowledge base
* Security visibly enabling revenue, with named regulated and public sector opportunities won or retained on the strength of our security position
* A prioritised information security risk register, owned by the business and reviewed at executive level
* Detection and response matured: consolidated tooling, tested playbooks, and time to detect and respond trending down

* A published position on AI security and acceptable use, with the AI estate inventoried and a clear approval route to be an enabler for innovation

***Certification & Compliance***

* Own delivery of SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 as a single efficient control programme
* Build and run the information security management system: policies, controls, evidence, internal audit and management review, and own the relationship with auditors and certification bodies

***Customer Assurance & Commercial Enablement***

* Run customer assurance: an external trust centre, a maintained questionnaire knowledge base, clear service levels back to Sales, and reporting on the commercial contribution of security

***Security Operations & Engineering***

* Own detection and response, and run vulnerability, exposure and patch management to agreed targets, with the external attack surface actively managed
* Own identity and access security with IT Operations & Platforms: privileged access, service accounts, conditional access, and joiner, mover and leaver controls
* Own the security tooling roadmap and budget, consolidating the estate as required

***Cloud, Product & Web Security***

* Secure Graitec's public estate, platforms and hosted services, setting secure-by-design standards for cloud landing zones, integrations and customer-facing services
* Extend remit to our intellectual property and product security, with a strong working interface into R&D
* Embed secure development practice with R&D: secure SDLC, code and dependency scanning, secrets management, and penetration testing with tracked remediation

***Risk, Resilience & Governance***

* Build and maintain the information security risk register, with business ownership, an agreed risk appetite and executive-level reporting
* Own third party and vendor security assessment, including periodic reassessment and secure offboarding, and provide security due diligence for acquisitions
* Drive security governance for corporate AI: inventory and approval of tools and agents, AI access to corporate data, AI vendor risk, and responsible use
* Own incident response and business continuity: run exercises, lead responses, and work with other functions on disaster recovery design and testing
* Build security awareness that changes behaviour, with targeted training, phishing simulation and a strong culture of prevention

  
**Responsibilities**

* Strong working knowledge of the Microsoft security stack (Defender, Entra ID, Purview, Sentinel) and of managing an outsourced or co-managed SOC
* Cloud security, including landing zones, identity, securing internet-facing services, and penetration testing and vulnerability remediation with R&D teams
* Security risk management, third party assurance and GDPR obligations, working alongside a Data Protection Officer
* AI security and governance: securing AI agents that access corporate data, and setting the inventory, approval and acceptable use framework
* Comfortable as the only dedicated security professional, pragmatic and proportionate in a mid-sized, fast-moving business
* Commercially astute, credible in front of customers, and able to translate risk into business language
* Self-directed and evidence-driven, taking work to completion, and able to develop junior talent and mature a small team

* Experience in M&A due diligence and integration, in an acquisitive or private equity-backed group
* Exposure to NIS2, DORA or the EU AI Act

  
**Qualifications**  
  

* Executive-level communication, with a track record of leading adoption and change across multinational, multidisciplinary teams
* Results-oriented mindset with a high degree of ownership and accountability.

# DevOps Engineer - C#

London, United Kingdom

JUXT is partnering with a global asset management firm to standardise and improve build and deployment pipelines across their application estate.

The estate is a mix of C# / .NET and Python services, with a long history of per-team build conventions, varied deployment targets, and tooling. The goal is a small set of opinionated, well-supported pipeline patterns that every team can adopt, with consistent quality gates, observability, and deployment behaviour. You will join a small, high-performing squad of DevOps engineers, working with the client and embedded alongside application teams to create clean, portable, repeatable build and deployment processes.

The client is a high-performing London Asset Management firm operating as part of a major international banking group, running a .NET-focused technical stack with an agile, collaborative culture.

This role suits a senior, delivery-focused engineer who genuinely enjoys the platform/enablement craft: making other engineers faster and safer by giving them sensible defaults rather than a wall of YAML. You should be opinionated about what good pipelines look like, pragmatic about meeting application teams where they actually are, and patient about migrating long-standing setups without breaking production.

Essential functions

You will work on:

* **Standardised pipeline templates.** Designing and building reusable GitHub Actions workflows that application teams can adopt with minimal bespoke work - covering build, test, scan, package, promote and deploy across pre-production and production environments.
* **Containerisation and 12-factor apps.** Working with application teams to package services as containers, externalise configuration, surface logs and metrics correctly, and remove the hidden assumptions about the underlying host that make migration painful.
* **Mixed deployment targets.** Supporting both Kubernetes and VM / Windows server deployment patterns within the same pipeline framework, so teams can adopt the standard regardless of where their service currently runs.
* **Quality and security gates.** Wiring test suites and tools like SonarQube, SAST / DAST tooling, dependency / CVE scanning and image signing into the standard pipeline so coverage and CVE thresholds are enforced by default.
* **Infrastructure as Code.** Authoring and reviewing Terraform / Bicep where the pipeline standard needs supporting infrastructure (build runners, environments, registries, identities).
* **Migration off legacy tooling.** Moving build pipelines from Azure DevOps pipelines onto the standardised GitHub Actions-based flow without losing production capability mid-flight.
* **Enablement.** Documenting the standard, supporting adopting teams, and raising the floor on what “good” looks like across the wider engineering organisation.

Qualifications

### Essential

* Hands-on DevOps engineer with substantial production experience designing and operating **Azure DevOps and Octopus Deploy**, at scale (reusable workflows, composite actions, matrix builds, self-hosted runners, environments and approvals).
* Real experience designing **continuous delivery pipelines** that promote a build through multiple pre-production environments to production, with appropriate gates, approvals and rollback behaviour.
* Comfortable working with **on-premise networking, firewalls and VM-based deployment targets**, and designing pipeline patterns that work for both without becoming a tangled mess.
* Strong instincts for **pipeline as a product**: templates and standards that other engineers actually want to adopt, with good defaults, clear extension points, and minimal cognitive load.
* High autonomy and strong written communication. You will be working with multiple application teams who have their own way of doing things - clarity and pragmatism matter as much as technical depth.

### Beneficial

* Experience with **GitHub Actions**.
* **Infrastructure as Code** experience, for the supporting infrastructure that pipelines and environments.
* Familiarity with the **12-factor app** principles in practice.
* Background wiring applications into **observability stacks** (Prometheus / Grafana, Datadog, Azure Application Insights) as a standard part of deployment.
* Experience integrating **security and supply-chain tooling** (SonarQube, ProGet, Snyk, image signing) into CI / CD as enforced gates.
* Reading-level familiarity with **C# / .NET** and / or **Python** - enough to understand and improve the build and test phases of the apps you’re pipelining, even if you’re not writing application code day to day.
