# Technical Programme Manager – Technology Estate & Modernisation

London, United Kingdom

JUXT (part of Grid Dynamics) is partnering with a leading global asset management firm to provide dedicated programme management for the initiatives that keep its technology estate healthy, secure and up to date.

The firm's IT and infrastructure teams manage a continuous stream of important technical initiatives, including:

* Decommissioning legacy infrastructure
* Upgrading software across the technology estate
* Remediating security vulnerabilities
* Improving automated test coverage and engineering quality
* Migrating systems into the wider parent banking group's environment
* Addressing accumulated technology debt

Historically, this work has often sat within individual technology teams without dedicated programme ownership.

This newly created **Technical Programme Manager (TPM)** role has been established to address that gap.

You will take ownership of these initiatives from initial scoping through to completion, creating structure around the work, coordinating the teams involved, identifying and removing blockers, and providing clear visibility to technology leadership.

You will join the firm's technology organisation in the **City of London**, working alongside an established TPM and closely with systems architecture leadership.

This is a hands-on technical programme management role. It is particularly suited to someone who is comfortable working directly with engineers, infrastructure specialists, architects and security teams and who enjoys understanding the technical detail behind delivery challenges.

Essential functions

## The Role

As Technical Programme Manager, you will own a portfolio of technology-focused initiatives and ensure that they make consistent progress through to completion.

You will not simply maintain project plans. You'll be expected to understand what needs to happen, establish the delivery approach, coordinate the relevant technical teams, challenge delays and dependencies, and provide senior stakeholders with a clear view of progress and risk.

The role sits at the intersection of **technology, engineering and delivery**.

Qualifications

## The Role

As Technical Programme Manager, you will own a portfolio of technology-focused initiatives and ensure that they make consistent progress through to completion.

You will not simply maintain project plans. You'll be expected to understand what needs to happen, establish the delivery approach, coordinate the relevant technical teams, challenge delays and dependencies, and provide senior stakeholders with a clear view of progress and risk.

The role sits at the intersection of **technology, engineering and delivery**.

### Key Responsibilities

Technology Debt & Modernisation

* Own technology debt initiatives from discovery and scoping through to completion.
* Establish clear objectives, scope, milestones and delivery plans.
* Coordinate engineering, infrastructure, architecture, security and application teams.
* Track progress against agreed milestones and proactively address slippage.
* Identify technical, organisational and dependency-related blockers.
* Ensure initiatives have clear ownership and accountable delivery teams.
* Maintain visibility of outstanding technology risks and remediation activity.

Infrastructure Decommissioning

* Drive programmes to retire obsolete infrastructure and technology components.
* Coordinate discovery and dependency analysis before decommissioning.
* Work with infrastructure and application teams to establish retirement plans.
* Track application, service and infrastructure dependencies.
* Coordinate migration, validation and shutdown activities.
* Ensure decommissioning activities are completed safely and with appropriate technical evidence.

Software Upgrade Programmes

* Coordinate large-scale software and platform upgrades across the technology estate.
* Establish upgrade roadmaps and delivery milestones.
* Work with engineering teams to identify affected applications and dependencies.
* Track adoption and remediation across multiple teams.
* Escalate risks where teams or systems are unable to meet upgrade deadlines.
* Coordinate testing, release and implementation activities where required.

Security & Vulnerability Remediation

* Coordinate remediation programmes arising from identified security vulnerabilities.
* Work closely with security, infrastructure and engineering teams to understand remediation requirements.
* Ensure vulnerabilities are appropriately prioritised and assigned.
* Track remediation through to deployment and closure.
* Identify blockers preventing teams from addressing vulnerabilities.
* Provide clear reporting on outstanding risks, remediation progress and dependencies.

Engineering Quality

* Drive initiatives designed to improve software engineering quality.
* Coordinate programmes such as improving automated test coverage.
* Work with engineering teams to understand current levels of coverage and identify gaps.
* Establish measurable objectives and delivery milestones.
* Track progress across applications and teams.
* Help ensure quality improvements become part of normal engineering delivery rather than isolated exercises.

Parent Banking Group Migration

* Support programmes migrating systems into the wider parent banking group's technology environment.
* Coordinate application, infrastructure, architecture, security and platform stakeholders.
* Track migration dependencies and readiness criteria.
* Manage delivery risks and issues across multiple technical teams.
* Ensure migration activities have clear ownership, milestones and completion criteria.

## Programme Governance & Reporting

A core part of the role will be establishing a consistent delivery cadence across the portfolio.

You will:

* Establish clear programme plans and delivery milestones.
* Maintain RAID logs covering risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies.
* Track actions and decisions through to completion.
* Produce concise status reporting for technology leadership.
* Highlight material risks and blockers early.
* Maintain clear dependency maps across teams and initiatives.
* Establish regular programme and stakeholder forums where appropriate.
* Ensure stakeholders understand what is progressing, what is blocked and what requires intervention.
* Provide evidence-based reporting rather than relying solely on subjective status updates.

The expectation is that reporting will be **clear, concise and actionable**.

## Technical Delivery

This is a technical programme management position rather than a traditional business transformation or change-management role.

You will be expected to engage with technical teams at a meaningful level and understand the substance behind delivery plans.

You should be comfortable asking questions such as:

* What is actually preventing this upgrade from being completed?
* Which applications depend on this infrastructure?
* What technical work remains before this system can be decommissioned?
* Is the vulnerability genuinely remediated, or has the risk simply been accepted or deferred?
* What environments need to be upgraded?
* What testing is required before release?
* Which team owns the remaining dependency?
* What architectural decision is blocking delivery?
* What evidence do we need to consider the initiative complete?

You won't necessarily be writing the code or implementing the infrastructure yourself, but you should be technically credible enough to understand the answers and challenge delivery assumptions when necessary.

## Stakeholder Management

You will work with a broad range of technical stakeholders, including:

* Software engineers
* Infrastructure engineers
* Platform teams
* Systems architects
* Security teams
* Application owners
* Technology leadership
* Engineering managers
* Programme and project managers
* Teams within the wider parent banking group

You will need to adapt your communication to different audiences while maintaining a consistent view of programme status.

At senior levels, this means communicating succinctly around:

**Progress → Risks → Dependencies → Decisions → Actions**

At engineering level, it means engaging in enough technical detail to understand what is actually required to deliver the work.

## What We're Looking For

### Essential Experience

* Proven experience working as a **Technical Programme Manager, Technical Project Manager or similar technical delivery role**.
* Experience running **IT, infrastructure or engineering initiatives**, rather than primarily business change programmes.
* Experience delivering initiatives such as:

  + Infrastructure decommissioning
  + Technology upgrades
  + Security remediation
  + Vulnerability remediation
  + Platform migrations
  + Technology modernisation
  + Engineering quality initiatives
* A strong technical background and the ability to work credibly with engineers and infrastructure teams.
* Experience managing multiple initiatives or workstreams simultaneously.
* Strong planning, tracking and organisational skills.
* Experience identifying and managing technical dependencies.
* Experience managing delivery risks and blockers.
* Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and take ownership of initiatives from inception through completion.
* Ability to communicate technical delivery status clearly to senior technology stakeholders.

### Technical Understanding

You don't need to be a hands-on engineer, but you should have sufficient technical depth to understand modern enterprise technology environments.

Relevant experience could include familiarity with:

* Infrastructure and cloud platforms
* Application architecture
* Software development lifecycles
* Enterprise applications
* APIs and distributed systems
* Databases
* Operating systems and infrastructure
* Networking
* Security vulnerabilities and remediation
* Software upgrades and patching
* Application migrations
* CI/CD and release processes
* Automated testing
* Technology lifecycle management

The precise technology stack is less important than your ability to understand technical delivery problems and work effectively with engineering teams.

Would be a plus

## Desirable Experience

Experience in any of the following would be beneficial:

* Financial services
* Asset management
* Investment banking
* Banking technology
* Highly regulated environments
* Large enterprise technology estates
* Technology debt programmes
* Legacy technology modernisation
* Infrastructure transformation
* Cloud migration
* Data-centre or infrastructure decommissioning
* Enterprise application migrations
* Cybersecurity remediation programmes
* Software lifecycle management
* Technology governance
* Working with architecture functions
* Working across multiple engineering teams
* Parent/subsidiary technology integration

## Personal Attributes

### Technically Credible

You can engage comfortably with engineers, architects and infrastructure specialists and understand the technical substance behind their delivery commitments.

### Organised

You can manage multiple concurrent initiatives without losing track of actions, dependencies, risks or deadlines.

### Self-Directed

You don't need a detailed instruction set to get started. You identify what needs to happen, establish structure and drive the work forward.

### Delivery-Focused

You care about outcomes and completion rather than simply maintaining project plans and producing status reports.

### Pragmatic

You understand that enterprise technology environments contain constraints and dependencies. You focus on finding practical routes through them.

### Clear Communicator

You can take a complicated technical situation and communicate the important facts clearly to both engineers and senior leadership.

### Collaborative

You build effective relationships across engineering, infrastructure, security, architecture and management teams.

### Persistent

Technology debt initiatives can involve long-running dependencies and competing priorities. You are comfortable maintaining momentum and following issues through to resolution.

## What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means establishing clear ownership and momentum across a portfolio of technical initiatives.

Within the role, you will help create:

* Clear visibility of technology debt and remediation work.
* Well-defined ownership for each initiative.
* Realistic delivery plans and milestones.
* Consistent tracking and reporting.
* Early identification of delivery risks.
* Effective management of cross-team dependencies.
* Faster resolution of technical blockers.
* Clear escalation when intervention is required.
* Successful completion of infrastructure decommissioning and upgrade programmes.
* Improved security remediation progress.
* Measurable improvements in engineering quality.
* Successful migration of systems into the parent banking group's environment.

Most importantly, the organisation should have confidence that important technical initiatives are being actively driven rather than sitting within individual teams without clear programme ownership.

## Working Environment

You will be embedded within the technology organisation of a leading global asset management firm.

You'll work closely with an established Technical Programme Manager and the systems architecture leadership team, while coordinating delivery across multiple technology functions.

The environment is likely to involve complex enterprise systems, legacy technology, multiple dependencies and competing engineering priorities.

This makes the ability to understand technical detail while maintaining a clear programme-level perspective particularly important.

## Location & Working Pattern

**Location:** City of London, UK

**Working model:** Hybrid

**Office attendance:** 3 days per week

The role requires regular interaction with technology teams and leadership, making in-person collaboration an important part of the engagement.

## Employment Options

JUXT is considering both:

* **Permanent employment**
* **Contract engagements**

Specific contractual arrangements and commercial terms will be discussed as part of the recruitment process.

## Why Join the Engagement?

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a newly established technical programme management function within a sophisticated financial-services technology environment.

Rather than managing a single conventional project, you will have responsibility for a portfolio of initiatives addressing some of the fundamental challenges of maintaining and modernising a large technology estate.

The role offers exposure to:

* Enterprise technology strategy
* Infrastructure modernisation
* Technology debt
* Cybersecurity remediation
* Software engineering
* Systems architecture
* Application migration
* Technology governance
* Financial-services technology

You'll also have the opportunity to establish delivery practices and bring greater structure and visibility to an important area of technology investment.

## Role Summary

JUXT is looking for a **Technical Programme Manager** to take end-to-end ownership of technology debt and modernisation initiatives for a leading global asset management firm.

The successful candidate will be a technically credible programme manager who understands engineering and infrastructure environments and can turn complex, distributed technical work into structured, measurable delivery programmes.

You will coordinate initiatives ranging from infrastructure decommissioning and software upgrades to vulnerability remediation, engineering quality improvements and migration into the wider parent banking group.

The role requires someone who is **organised, technically credible, self-directed and delivery-focused**, with the ability to work effectively with engineers while providing concise and reliable visibility to technology leadership.

# **Director, Pipeline & Portfolio Strategy, Europe & International, ViiV**

  

**Why ViiV**

ViiV Healthcare is the only company 100% focused on HIV. Our purpose is to get ahead of HIV together, our ambition is to help end the HIV and AIDS epidemic, and our mission is to leave no person living with HIV behind.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the future of ViiV’s portfolio across a large and diverse region, influence choices at the intersection of science and commercial strategy and help bring meaningful innovation to people living with and at risk of HIV.  
  
  
**Position Summary**  
ViiV Healthcare is entering a critical period of portfolio evolution. Sustaining growth requires optimizing pipeline strategy across the Europe and International region, to inform robust pipeline decisions for future innovation on HIV treatment and prevention medications, together with disciplined launch footprint planning to unlock value across a diverse Europe & International region.

The Director, Pipeline & Portfolio Strategy will be the senior regional commercial lead for pipeline and portfolio strategy. The role will shape regional perspectives on asset potential, portfolio choices, launch sequencing and investment priorities, and will translate those choices into aligned action across Global, Regional and local market teams.

**Job purpose**

To own and lead the Europe & International commercial pipeline and launch strategy, ensuring that ViiV makes clear, evidence-based choices on future assets, lifecycle opportunities, launch readiness and regional investment. The role will provide recommendations for Regional Leadership Team and Global governance decisions, strengthen portfolio discipline across markets, and maximise long-term value and patient impact.

**Key accountabilities**

* **Regional pipeline and launch strategy**. Define and maintain an integrated, future-facing commercial view of ViiV’s pipeline, and launch sequencing across Europe & International, aligned to enterprise and regional priorities, optimizing pipeline value.
* **Shape global and regional decisions**. Develop an evidence-based strategy for regional recommendations on asset prioritisation, launch sequencing, market archetypes, lifecycle choices and investment trade-offs. Providing the Europe & International commercial perspective for relevant global asset, franchise and governance forums, providing clear recommendations grounded in market potential, patient need, access realities, competitive dynamics and execution feasibility.
* **Direct early commercial strategy for pipeline assets**. Lead regional commercial input from early development through pre-launch, including target product and value proposition considerations, market shaping needs, evidence gaps, customer insights and critical success factors.
* **Lead insight-led scenario planning**. Integrate market research, competitive intelligence, epidemiology, access and policy developments, financial scenarios and local market insight to assess uncertainty and guide portfolio decisions.
* **Provide enterprise-level matrix leadership**. Lead and align senior stakeholders across Commercial, Medical, Market Access, Regulatory, R&D, Finance, Insights & Analytics, CGA, Global and LOC teams, creating clarity on decisions, ownership, milestones and escalation.

**Decision-making and autonomy**

* **Portfolio decision leadership**. Leads the regional process and recommendation for pipeline and portfolio prioritization and launch sequencing, for material decisions and investment choices taken at the appropriate Regional or Global governance forum.
* **High autonomy**. Operates with significant autonomy, working across a complex matrix remit, to define the regional pipeline and launch plans.
* **Executive escalation**. Escalates choices carrying material commercial, financial, legal, regulatory or reputational implications to the Head of E&I Pipeline and the relevant leadership or governance body as required.
* **Regional authority**. Acts as the accountable regional commercial point of view for assigned pipeline and portfolio matters, while respecting functional decision rights and governance requirements.

**Scope and impact**

* **Regional breadth**. Above-country responsibility across Europe & International, which is all markets outside US. Encompassing direct local operating companies and Alliance markets with differing epidemiology, access models, competitive environments and commercial maturity.
* **Business impact**. Shapes choices that influence long-range growth, the value realised from future assets, the quality and speed of launch readiness, and the allocation of regional capacity and investment.
* **Leadership reach**. Leads through a senior cross-functional matrix across a complex region.
* **Executive visibility**. Provides regular recommendations, pipeline portfolio strategy, plans and decision materials to Regional Leadership Team members and contributes to relevant Global governance discussions.

  

**Why You?**  
*We will love your high accountability for impact performance, your ambition for patients and strategic curiosity, and your collaboration and influence abilities. Your passion for our mission and purpose of getting ahead of HIV together will enthuse us! How you work is as important as what you deliver.*

**Knowledge, experience and qualifications**

* Extensive senior commercial leadership experience in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare or a closely related sector, with significant exposure to portfolio strategy, pipeline commercialisation, launch excellence or lifecycle management.

The Senior Manager, Advanced Analytics, AI & Digital Solutions is responsible for leading delivery of the Digital Foundry portfolio and ensuring AI, modelling, optimisation, and digital solutions are successfully translated from strategy into measurable business outcomes.

  

Reporting to the Director, Supply Chain AI Solutions, the role acts as the delivery leader for Digital Foundry initiatives, converting portfolio priorities into executable roadmaps, coordinating multidisciplinary delivery teams, and ensuring successful deployment, adoption, and value realisation across the portfolio.

  

The successful candidate will combine strong business understanding, technical credibility, product delivery expertise, and people leadership capabilities to drive execution of high-value digital solutions across Quality and Supply Chain.

  
  

**What You'll Do**

**Lead Solution Delivery**

* Lead coordinated execution and delivery of approved Digital Foundry initiatives from solution concept through development, deployment, adoption, and benefits realisation.
* Translate portfolio priorities and value objectives into executable product roadmaps, delivery plans, release schedules, and resource requirements.
* Manage multiple initiatives across the Digital Foundry portfolio.
* Ensure delivery milestones, outcomes, benefits, and adoption targets are achieved.
* Remove delivery barriers and proactively manage risks, dependencies, and escalations across initiatives.

**Product & Portfolio Management**

* Lead product planning, backlog management, prioritisation, and release planning across the portfolio.
* Oversee delivery execution from initiation through deployment and operational adoption.
* Ensure alignment between business priorities, technical delivery activities, and value-realisation objectives.
* Support portfolio governance, delivery reporting, and benefits-tracking activities.
* Balance competing priorities, resources, and delivery capacity to maximise overall portfolio value.

**Technical Leadership**

* Provide technical and product delivery leadership across AI, optimisation, modelling, simulation, analytics, and digital solutions.
* Direct and oversee development activities delivered by Digital Foundry teams.
* Review solution approaches and ensure alignment with architecture, standards, quality expectations, scalability requirements, and business objectives.
* Promote reusable solutions, delivery best practices, and technical excellence.
* Ensure effective application of machine learning, optimisation, simulation, generative AI, and emerging digital capabilities.

**Business Partnership**

* Partner with business leaders and the Director, Supply Chain AI Solutions to refine priority opportunities into clearly defined use cases, delivery requirements, and measurable outcomes.
* Facilitate discovery workshops, solution planning activities, and delivery reviews.
* Communicate delivery progress, value, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations to stakeholders.
* Support successful adoption and business integration of Digital Foundry solutions.
* Ensure stakeholders remain aligned on scope, priorities, benefits, and delivery expectations.

**Team Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop technical team members across analytics, AI, modelling, and digital solution disciplines.
* Set objectives, manage performance, develop capability, and build succession pipelines across the Digital Foundry team.
* Build capability in digital product delivery, technical leadership, and solution execution.
* Plan and deploy internal and external delivery capacity across the portfolio.
* Balance specialist capability requirements with business priorities and delivery commitments.
* Foster collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and high-performance team behaviours.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Reliable delivery of the Digital Foundry portfolio.
* Strong business adoption of deployed solutions.
* High-performing technical and delivery teams.
* Effective prioritisation and backlog management.
* Consistent delivery of measurable business value.
* Successful conversion of approved opportunities into scaled, sustainable digital solutions.

  

**Qualifications & Skills**

**Essential**

* Significant experience delivering analytics, AI, modelling, optimisation, digital transformation, or technology-enabled business solutions.
* Proven experience leading a portfolio of concurrent analytics, AI, modelling, or digital-product initiatives from planning through deployment and adoption.
* Strong understanding of supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, or related business domains.
* Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary technical and cross-functional delivery teams.
* Experience establishing product roadmaps, prioritised backlogs, release plans, and measurable delivery outcomes.
* Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities and value objectives into executable delivery plans.
* Experience managing delivery dependencies, risks, resources, and competing priorities.
* Experience translating business requirements into scalable digital solutions.
* Strong stakeholder management, influencing, and communication skills.
* Experience working within agile or product-centric delivery environments.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
* Experience with modern analytics, AI, modelling, optimisation, or cloud-based technology platforms.

**Preferred**

* Degree in Data Science, Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Supply Chain, Operations Research, or related discipline.
* Advanced degree preferred.
* Experience in consumer healthcare, FMCG, manufacturing, or complex supply chain environments.

**Finance Assistant - Accounts Payable**

At Halfords, our mission is to inspire and support a lifetime of motoring and cycling. As a specialist retailer, we lead the market through customer-driven innovation and a distinct product range. We are dedicated to providing our customers with an integrated, unique, and convenient service experience - from e-bike and electric vehicle servicing to on-demand solutions. Our commitment is to foster customer loyalty by offering compelling reasons to keep coming back to our stores, ensuring a lifetime of motoring and cycling enjoyment.

**About the role**

Join our Finance Shared Services team and play a key role in ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time, helping to keep our garage operations running smoothly. You'll be responsible for processing invoices, resolving supplier and payment queries, reconciling accounts, and building strong relationships with both suppliers and internal stakeholders.

This is a fast-paced role suited to someone with excellent attention to detail, strong organisational skills, and previous Accounts Payable experience. You'll have the opportunity to contribute to continuous improvement initiatives while developing your finance knowledge within a supportive and evolving team environment.

**At Halfords, we operate a hybrid working policy with 2 days on site at our Support Centre in Redditch.**

**Key responsibilities**

* Manage the end-to-end Accounts Payable process, ensuring supplier invoices are processed accurately and payments are made on time.
* Build strong relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders, resolving invoice, payment, and purchase order queries efficiently.
* Reconcile supplier accounts, investigate discrepancies and historic balances, and support audit requirements where needed.
* Support operational teams with invoice matching and reporting, helping to improve compliance and resolve issues across the garage network.
* Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and help drive best practice within the Finance Shared Services team.

**About you**

* Previous experience in a Financial or Accounts Payable role - **Advantageous, not essential**
* Strong time management skills with a "get up and go" attitude towards problem solving and working to deadlines
* SAP knowledge is **advantageous, but not essential**
* Strong knowledge of MS Office applications **(Mostly Excel, SharePoint & Teams)**
* Strong communication skill- especially with key stakeholders both in person and telephone

**Reward & benefits**

* A fair and competitive salary evaluated against market data, annual discretionary bonus scheme, pension, life assurance, 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave.

* Commitment and dedication to your ongoing personal and professional development. We help you to own and grow your potential so you can be at your best in your current role and to support your future career aspirations.

* You will have access to a wealth of employee discounts across the Halfords suite of products and services.

* Wellbeing and inclusion are at the heart of our colleague experience. We offer resources and ongoing support to enhance your wellbeing at work and active Colleague Networks supporting inclusion initiatives across Halfords.

As a Business Data Analyst, you'll become a key member of Hallmark’s Data & Analytics Centre of Excellence, helping to transform the way we use data to support decision-making across the business. Working closely with key stakholders across the business you'll deliver practical analytics, robust reporting and data-driven recommendations that help turn insight into action.

You'll play an important role in helping us uncover the story behind the data, joining the dots across multiple business functions and translating complex analysis into clear, decision-ready insight. This is an exciting opportunity to make a real impact, combining business-critical reporting with analytical project work that supports performance improvement and drives meaningful change.

Your Responsibilities

* Deliver insights through analytical reports, dashboards and project work, using data to answer business questions and identify opportunities to improve performance.
* Support the Reporting & Analytics Manager and key stakeholders by providing data-led analysis that improves understanding of business drivers, trends and outcomes.
* Lead and support recurring market and customer analytics activity, including market analysis, product reviews and post-season performance reviews.
* Deliver analytical projects that support business decision-making, including sales performance analysis, missed opportunity reviews, target setting, stock allocation and product or range performance evaluations.
* Use analytical tools and technologies to improve reporting processes, reduce manual effort and increase the reliability and efficiency of recurring analysis.
* Partner with teams across Creative, Product, Commercial, Ecommerce, Supply and Finance to understand requirements, define scope and identify opportunities to generate greater value from data.
* Help maintain clear documentation, standards and processes to ensure analytics activity remains repeatable, reliable and scalable.
* Support wider Data & Analytics activity and provide cover for key reporting and analytical responsibilities when required.

Your Accountabilities

* Delivering accurate, relevant and well-documented analytical reports, dashboards and projects that support business decision-making.
* Translating data into clear recommendations, actionable insights and meaningful business intelligence.
* Identifying trends, risks, opportunities and key performance drivers, helping stakeholders understand the factors influencing business outcomes.
* Improving the efficiency, consistency and scalability of recurring analytical processes through effective use of reporting tools and documented ways of working.
* Ensuring stakeholders understand the scope, limitations and confidence levels of analytical outputs to support informed decision-making.
* Contributing to the delivery of business performance improvements through proactive identification of opportunities and data-led recommendations.

To Be Successful You Will Need

* Experience in an analytical role, either within a dedicated Data & Analytics function or a Commercial, Product, Insight or Merchandising environment.
* Strong communication skills, with the ability to understand business questions and present insights in a clear and compelling way.
* Experience using Business Intelligence tools, ideally Tableau, including building, interpreting and explaining analytical outputs.
* Advanced Excel skills, including working with large datasets, validating outputs and presenting insights effectively.
* Strong PowerPoint and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complex analysis into impactful recommendations.
* Adaptability and a solutions-focused mindset, with the ability to deliver insights at pace while understanding data quality and limitations.
* Curiosity and a passion for using data to solve business problems.
* A collaborative approach, with a willingness to support colleagues, share knowledge and contribute to team success.
* Experience of Snowflake, SQL, Alteryx or similar analytical tools would be advantageous.
* A desire to continuously develop your analytical and technical capabilities and help others gain value from data

As a Visual Merchandiser (Planner), you’ll play a key role in bringing our customer‐focused creative vision and commercialised range builds to life at store level across all formats and channels. Working closely with Product & Range Managers and wider commercial teams, you’ll support the preparation and execution of customer range builds, system setup and store‐level planning activity.

You’ll contribute to Hallmark’s business objectives by ensuring stores are visually consistent, compliant and ready to trade. Through accurate planning, data‐led insight and strong operational support, you’ll help enable effective store execution and customer impact.

## **Your Responsibilities**

* Understand retailer strategy, creative vision and commercial KPIs, translating ranging strategies into store‐level planograms by mission, format and channel.
* Use display planning software, including Card Manager, to execute all planogram cascades.
* Build from Largest and Most Common range builds using system‐led product ranking.
* Load and maintain store plans, planograms and stock allocations using planning tools such as Card Manager, Link5 and Order Pool.
* Support store refits, fixture changes and new launches by producing accurate documentation and clearly communicating with internal teams and third‐party partners.
* Keep planogram, fixture and store information up to date throughout the product lifecycle, from launch through to exit.
* Produce and maintain weekly and ad‐hoc reports to support decision‐making across Visual Merchandising, Customer Operations and Commercial teams.
* Action plan‐level pocket amendments to optimise stock availability and performance.
* Translate store plans and layouts into clear, user‐friendly formats for third‐party merchandisers and external partners.
* Maintain store plan libraries, POS matrices and compliance image banks, identifying and resolving inaccuracies with key stakeholders.

## **Your Accountabilities**

* Delivery of accurate and timely store‐level plans.
* Ongoing SKU‐level maintenance and system accuracy.
* High standards of data capture, integrity and version control across all planning systems.
* Adherence to Critical Date Paths to support launches, refits and range changes.
* Providing reliable operational support to enable wider teams to meet commercial and customer objectives.
* Building and maintaining strong relationships across internal departments and stakeholders.
* Identifying opportunities for continuous improvement in systems, processes and ways of working.

## **To Be Successful You Will Need**

* Experience working with large datasets and strong Excel skills, including pivot tables and VLOOKUPs (essential); Power Query and Macros (desirable).
* Experience using Card Manager or similar planning tools (desirable).
* Strong systems capability with confidence troubleshooting issues and implementing solutions.
* Experience in an administrative or planning‐related role, managing workloads, deadlines and Critical Date Paths (essential).
* High attention to detail with a structured, problem‐solving mindset.
* Ability to prioritise effectively and work to deadlines across multiple timelines.
* Clear and confident communication skills, with a collaborative approach across teams.

# Deputy Branch Manager - Swindon

## Job Introduction

Handelsbanken offers a genuinely different approach to banking. We are a local relationship bank providing bespoke, customer-led banking and wealth management services for personal and corporate customers. 

Our branch teams build trusted, long-term relationships with customers in their local communities. With our decentralised ways of working, decisions are made in the branch, close to the customers. Teams decide who they work with and how best to support them, without short-term sales targets or bonus-driven incentives. Instead, we focus on doing what is right for the customer, even when that means prioritising long-term value over short-term profit.

This approach has underpinned our success for decades. Today, Handelsbanken holds the strongest credit rating among its peer banks, is independently recognised as Europe’s safest commercial bank, and is consistently ranked highly for customer satisfaction and relationship banking, 

Our culture is values-led, shaped by trust, respect, and long-term thinking. We empower our people to use their expertise, make confident decisions and build long-term careers. We look for people who share our long- term vision, want to grow and want to make a meaningful impact in their local community and with the Bank. 

We also recognise that flexibility can support people to perform at their best, and that it looks different for everyone. While arrangements will depend on the requirements of the role and the needs of the business, we are open to having a conversation around what flexibility could look like for you.

Check our Handelsbanken website for further information

The Deputy Branch Manager role is pivotal to Handelsbanken’s decentralised model and requires a developing leader who thrives on autonomy, accountability, and long-term relationship banking.

**Key responsibilities**

Strategic Leadership & Branch Performance

* Work closely with the Branch Manager and assist in leading the branch taking accountability for strategy, growth, and sustainable profitability to deliver consistently high levels of customer service and satisfaction.
* Assist and contribute toward the setting and delivery of the branch business plan, aligning commercial objectives with Handelsbanken’s values, customer-centric approach, and risk appetite.
* Translate local market insight into clear priorities and measurable outcomes to support long-term growth.
* Support the Branch Manager in ensuring the branch operates effectively within its defined geographical area, respecting the integrity of Handelsbanken’s local banking model.

City of London; Uxbridge

We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. The Compensation team leads compensation programs for Hasbro. Our work impacts every employee globally through the programs we coordinate. The team also has a meaningful role to play by ensuring our employee value proposition is competitive in the marketplace and financially balanced. We are looking for a Senior Compensation Analyst to lead this effort across EMEA and APAC. The incumbent shall partner closely with local HR teams and leaders to build and implement compensation programs. This role will provide direction and strategic solutions for compensation matters considering both business and HR priorities, market practices, and emerging trends.

**A day in the life of a Senior Compensation Analyst:**

* Lead compensation programs including but not limited to; market benchmarking reviews, compensation planning, recognition programs, offer development, retention programs, and budget management.
* Play a meaningful role in advising and educating key business stakeholders, HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on our compensation philosophy, to include the following components: base, variable, sales and equity compensation, as well as cyclical and ad-hoc compensation programs.
* Partner and collaborate closely with vital team members and client groups to understand organizational needs and prioritize accordingly. Providing compensation insights to support strategic decisions.
* Proactively assess internal and external trends, relevant pay legislation, market intelligence, and potential impact to our pay philosophy including our pay transparency projects.
* Provide consultation, mentoring and sophisticated advice to HR Business Partners and business leaders.
* Partner with Finance teams to craft and develop incentive plans, and support formal plan governance and oversight activities.
* Represent the voice of the customer in the design of enterprise-wide pay programs and lead the design for client pay program.
* Operate with a high degree of autonomy in managing compensation programs and analyses, applying sound judgment while ensuring alignment with company guidelines and governance standards.

**What you'll bring:**

* Bachelors or equivalent; proven track record in compensation.
* Experience crafting, developing and owning a variety of compensation programs and processes including base salary, variable pay programs, sales compensation, compensation strategy and competitive pay analysis.
* Deep analytical skills with an ability to break down sophisticated questions / data into well-structured analyses and synthesize key points.

# Evidence and Data Lead

#### We're looking for someone to help grow and deliver our evidence, evaluation and data work.

**Evidence & Data Lead**

*We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and are committed to celebrating and supporting diversity. We know we will thrive on it for the benefit of our employees, our products and services, and our community.  We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and particularly welcome applications from people with experiences of homelessness.*

**IN A NUTSHELL**

The Centre for Homelessness Impact is looking for an Evidence & Data Lead to help grow and deliver our evidence, evaluation and data work.

We are particularly looking for someone with strong quantitative skills who is comfortable working with numbers and complex datasets, designing and quality-assuring impact evaluations, and translating statistical findings into clear insights for policy and practice.

The ideal candidate will have a range of quantitative and evaluation tools and methods that they can deploy flexibly depending on the question at hand. This could include designing and overseeing Randomised Controlled Trials and quasi-experimental evaluations; analysing administrative, survey and financial data; undertaking statistical analysis; and critically assessing and synthesising evidence.

Candidates will have a knack for translating their findings into simple, yet meaningful messages for policy, service design, innovation and improvements on the data infrastructure.

Evidence and Data Leads work in close collaboration with the Director of Evidence to scope opportunities for our evidence and work and capitalise on opportunities for collaboration with other organisations in this space.

We are a small and focused team with great ambitions. We are looking for people with an entrepreneurial spirit - a self-starter who gets excited by uncovering insights and sees how they can be used to unlock new opportunities.

We work with multiple partners on a variety of projects - so it is crucial that the Evidence and Data  Leads are capable of prioritising effectively and devoting resources to the activities that are likely to generate the greatest impact.

**WHY IS THIS ROLE IMPORTANT FOR THE CENTRE’S WORK?**

At the Centre, we help people harness the power of evidence and data to improve policies and interventions to support people experiencing homelessness.

You will help shape the direction of our evidence work. This is a crucial stage of our journey as we expand our data and VFM work, and sustain momentum around our portfolio of evidence generation, particularly the delivery of the Test & Learn and Systems-Wide Evaluation programme.

Working under the oversight of the Director of Evidence, you will work across a portfolio of evaluations and data projects. You will oversee commissioned studies as well as undertake and quality-assure quantitative analysis in-house, working with administrative, survey and other datasets to generate insights relevant to homelessness policy and services. You will be responsible for ensuring methodological and statistical rigour, as well as policy relevance.

Most importantly, you will ensure those lessons are captured and fed into all the other streams of our work. Your skillset is critical to our work because you have the ability to both cultivate relationships with stakeholders and support the development of world-class researchers.

**WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO CAN**

Focus on Impact Evaluation:

* Manage the development and delivery of primary studies, particularly Randomised Controlled Trials and quasi-experimental evaluations, providing technical quality assurance across study design, sampling and power, outcome measurement, statistical analysis plans, implementation, analysis and reporting.
* Critically review quantitative analyses produced by evaluation partners, including statistical models, effect estimates, confidence intervals, subgroup analyses, missing data and attrition, and assess whether conclusions are supported by the evidence.
* Undertake quantitative analysis directly where required, including exploratory and descriptive analysis and, where appropriate, causal or quasi-experimental analysis.
* Support project sites as needed to support implementation, troubleshoot delivery issues, and maintain strong relationships with participating delivery partners.
* Play a key role in scoping new primary studies.
* Conduct independent applied research to inform organisational projects, policy engagement, and service design, including rapid evidence assessments, literature reviews, and analyses focused on specific populations or emerging issues related to homelessness.
* Provide expert advice across to partners by synthesising research findings and translating evidence into actionable insights for initiatives, evidence awareness, and dissemination, including evidence and data coaching sessions

Focus on Data Analysis:

* Manage quantitative data projects from beginning to end, including scoping analytical questions, assessing data quality, cleaning and linking datasets, undertaking statistical analysis and communicating findings.
* Analyse administrative, survey, financial and other quantitative datasets to identify trends, variation, inequalities and opportunities for improving homelessness services and systems.
* Use appropriate statistical techniques to answer policy questions, and be able to explain the assumptions, limitations and uncertainty associated with the analysis.
* Monitor national statistical releases, assess data quality and limitations, identify trends and cohort patterns, and produce analysis for CHI publications and stakeholder engagement.
* Develop clear and reproducible analytical outputs, using statistical software such as R, Python, Stata or equivalent, and present findings effectively through tables, charts and other data visualisations.

All candidates:

* Write concise and actionable summaries of insights for policymakers and practitioners that distil what we know works (Evidence Notes, blogs, and others); and take an active role in the dissemination of findings in multiple formats (presentations to senior policy and practical audiences, social media, etc);
* Manage the day-to-day development of some of our Evidence Tools (Intervention Tool, Evidence and Gap Maps, Evidence Finder), providing technical quality assurance at every stage of the project;
* Work in close collaboration with the Director of Evidence and Data to help develop and shape the Centre’s research agenda, contributing to scope, plan, and deliver new research, including delivering workshops, theory-of-change sessions, coaching, and tailored support to practitioners and local authorities to apply evidence in practice;
* Work closely with members of the Implementation Team to engage with homelessness practitioners to use evidence and data and with members of the Comms Team to support the dissemination of findings to our wider audience.
* Manage multiple projects and diverse stakeholders’ needs effectively and sensitively; with the capacity to build and nurture good relationships with diverse stakeholders including central government departments, local authorities, service providers, philanthropic organisations, and national sector bodies.
* Represent the organisation in external forums, cross-government working groups, and professional events, contributing expert input on evidence and data relating to homelessness.
* Flexibility to contribute to CHI’s other strands of work in a small, focused team; with openness to critique from other disciplines and curiosity to learn from the spectrum of perspectives represented by different members of the team and other stakeholders.
* Be a go-to source of quantitative expertise within CHI, helping colleagues interpret data, statistical findings and evaluation results and ensuring that quantitative claims made in our work are robust and appropriately communicated.

**RELEVANT EXPERIENCE AND BEHAVIOURS**

We need a self-starter, capable of scoping and delivering evidence-and-data-led projects and articulating effectively how these are aligned with our strategic priorities and the needs of decision-makers.

**Your experience includes:**

* Strong quantitative research skills, gained through a relevant discipline such as statistics, economics, epidemiology, quantitative social science, data science or a related field.
* Substantial experience analysing quantitative data and applying statistical methods to real-world policy or programme questions.
* Experience designing, delivering and/or quality-assuring impact evaluations, particularly Randomised Controlled Trials and quasi-experimental designs.
* Strong statistical literacy, including the ability to interpret effect sizes, uncertainty, confidence intervals, statistical significance, missing data, attrition and statistical model outputs.
* Practical experience using at least one statistical programming package such as R, Python, Stata or equivalent.
* Experience working with administrative, survey or other complex datasets, including assessing data quality and limitations.
* Experience managing complex research or evaluation projects involving multiple stakeholders.
* Ability to translate complex quantitative findings into clear and proportionate messages for decision-makers.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience using a range of economic evaluation methods such as Cost-Benefit, Cost-Consequences, Value for Money Frameworks, etc
* Experience in systematic reviews and rapid evidence assessments.
* Nuanced understanding of homelessness policies across the UK.
* Nuanced understanding of local authorities' financial data.
* Experience analysing linked or longitudinal administrative data.
* Experience with causal inference or quasi-experimental methods.
* Experience with data visualisation and reproducible analytical workflows.
* Experience using routinely collected government or local authority data.
* Experience undertaking or quality-assuring economic analysis.

**You will be able to demonstrate the following:**

* Ability to push the boundaries for how data and evidence can generate insights and contribute to designing intelligent services and systems to improve the lives of people experiencing homelessness or a risk.
* Ability to set clear priorities and work to tight deadlines

* Commitment to both the aims and values of the Centre.
* Openness to critique from other disciplines and curiosity to learn from various perspectives.

**About the role:**

* Deputise for the Senior Manager BCFOI to protect HS2 Ltd’s reputation internally and externally by ensuring that the transparency obligations within the Freedom of Information Act 2000 (FOI) and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR) are fully discharged in a timely manner and comply with the service level agreements (SLAs) set by the Department for Transport (DfT) and the Independent Commissioner’s Office (ICO).
* Deputise for the Senior Manager BCFOI as the principal HS2 Ltd authority on FOI and EIR, provide strategic and expert advice to senior colleagues, including HS2 Executive members and the CEO Office on relevant legislation in response to briefings and FOI requests (for example on Section 36 notices which must be issued by the CEO).
* Deputise for the Senior Manager BCFOI in managing the relationships between HS2 Ltd and other key external stakeholders including the Information Commissioner’s Office, the correspondence team in the Department for Transport, Members of Parliament, and Peers, to ensure the legally compliant, consistent, and coherent delivery of an efficient BCFOI service.
* Oversee and manage the day-to-day process for and caseload of the Briefings, Correspondence & FOI (BCFOI) team in discharging the company’s statutory duties regarding Freedom of Information (FOI) and Environmental Information Regulation (EIR) requests, HS2 Ltd’s Publication Scheme, written Parliamentary Questions, Correspondence (to the HS2 Ltd Chair and CEO), Ministerial correspondence and the Parliamentary Advice Line.

* Develop and maintain an overview of the issues and risks raised by stakeholders, identifying and feeding back into the business key risks and opportunities.
* Develop and run an awareness and training programme across the business, ensuring two-way understanding of the briefings, correspondence and freedom of information, Environmental Information Regulations and vother related statutory requirements on HS2 Ltd, learning and sharing lessons from the Information Commissioners Office (ICO) and Tribunal decisions and developing best practice.
* Lead the administration and management of the HS2 senior stakeholder speaker engagement programme.
* Work as part of the BCFOI/Public Affairs rota, performing on-call out of hours duties when required.

**About You:**

**Skills:**

* Management skills in leading teams to achieve set deliverables within tight deadlines to specified standards.
* Influencing and negotiation skills with both internal and external audiences, including at senior level.
* Ability to deliver quality, accurate and targeted communications at a senior level, internally and externally – including drafting communications for a variety of channels, representing an organisation with the ability to conduct/facilitate workshops and training sessions.
* Advisory skills at senior level internally and externally on complex matters in the application of legislation and official guidance.
* Stakeholder management at an internal and external senior level - with the ability to adapt to different audiences and deal with difficult stakeholders particularly in a complex political and challenging environment.
* Analytical skills, including the ability to collate, interpret and present complex information with clarity and consistency.
* Organisational and planning skills, with the ability to work to agreed deadlines in an agile environment.
* Problem resolution skills, with the ability to identify issues and exercise judgement to solve complex problems, and lead escalation as required.
* Ability to handle confidential information sensitively and discretely.
* Proficient in Microsoft Office programmes, especially Excel

**Knowledge:**

* Political awareness and understanding of matters relating to HS2.
* Knowledge of the planning and parliamentary process.
* Understanding of corporate communications, community engagement best practice, internal communications, social media, public relations, media relations, and customer complaints processes.
* Detailed knowledge of the principles and application of the Freedom of Information Act, the Environmental Information Regulations (EIR), the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) and associated legislation, guidance, and codes of practice.
* Understanding of government communications processes.
* Understanding of customer relationship management (CRM) databases.
* Knowledge of transport and/or major infrastructure projects.

**Experience:**

* Experience in managing and supporting teams in responding to briefings, correspondence and freedom of information requests with multiple stakeholders, including at senior level, internally and externally to meet statutory requirements
* Experience of managing teams to deliver briefings and correspondence information and requests to meet statutory requirements within tight deadlines.
* Experience in managing FOI/EIR requests (and the requirements of the FOI Act 2000 and EIR 2004).
* Experience of managing financial, policy and technical concepts to deliver accessible and accurate briefings and FOI correspondence.
* Experience in managing, processing and handling sensitive data and enquiries in a challenging environment.
* Experience in developing persuasive content for use across a range of communications channels.

The post-holder is expected to behave at all times in a manner consistent with the HS2 values of Safety, Leadership, Integrity and Respect.

* Support the adoption of new tools, processes and ideas.

* Strong decision-making skills, both within and out with areas of expertise.

When you join us at FPS, you are part of a much larger family. INEOS is a truly global company, with a diverse portfolio of businesses ranging from petrochemicals and healthcare to consumer brands and sports interests. **Our products touch and enhance every aspect of modern life**.

The Forties Pipeline System (FPS) plays a key role in safely and reliably transporting hydrocarbons from the central North Sea, onshore for processing.

Before commencing work with Ineos FPS you will need to complete our pre-employment screening process. This will consist of a pre-employment medical, employment history reference and qualification verification check. Some roles may also require a criminality check.

# Country Intelligence Lead Analyst - Latin America

Croydon, England, United Kingdom

Janes empowers military, government, and defense leaders to act with confidence in an increasingly complex world. Our trusted defense, security, and geopolitical information delivered through seamless digital platforms and system integrations—turns overwhelming data into clear, actionable intelligence and insight. By filling critical information gaps, Janes helps customers analyze threats, accelerate decisions, and stay ahead of emerging challenges.

**Job purpose:** 

The Lead Analyst will lead the Country Intelligence **Latin America** desk, managing and developing a team of analysts responsible for OSINT intelligence coverage across the region. This is a senior analytical and client-facing role requiring extensive knowledge of Mexican Non-State and Armed Groups (NSAGs) and Serious and Organised Crime data as well as a strong understanding of the wider Latin American security and geopolitical environment.

The successful candidate will be a recognised Mexico specialist, fluent in Spanish, and have a well-developed network of regional contacts and sources. They will bring considerable proven experience from a comparable intelligence, security, defence, government, risk or research environment and be able to engage with senior clients and stakeholders.

The position will also have a strong focus on the evolving US–Mexico security relationship and the strategic importance of Mexico within the wider Americas. Relevant issues include organised crime and cartel activity, narcotics trafficking, security cooperation, political and institutional stability, and changes in US and Mexican policy that may affect the regional security environment.

The Lead Analyst will drive the maintenance and enhancement of foundational country intelligence, including Political, Military, Economic, Social, Information and Infrastructure (PMESII) assessments, CBN coverage, NSAG profiles, and serious and organised crime content. They will monitor developments, commission and produce analysis, review the work of their team, and deliver written assessments in accordance with Janes' rigorous analytical standards.

As a senior subject-matter expert, the successful candidate will also represent Janes with customers and other external stakeholders.

The Country Intelligence Lead Analyst - Latin America – Latin America will report to the Principal Analyst, Latin America, NATO and Europe.

**How you will contribute at Janes:** 

* Lead Janes' open-source intelligence research and analysis on national security, geopolitical and stability risks across Latin America, with particular responsibility for Mexico.
* Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on Mexico, with particular expertise in NSAGs, cartels, serious and organised crime, security institutions and the political-security environment.
* Maintain and expand a trusted network of relevant regional contacts and sources to strengthen Janes' understanding of developments in Mexico and Latin America.
* Lead the updating and enhancement of foundational intelligence products, ensuring coverage reflects current intelligence priorities, emerging threats and changes in the regional security environment.
* Manage, mentor and develop analysts, setting research priorities, allocating work and ensuring consistently high analytical and editorial standards.
* Review and quality-assure analytical output, challenging assumptions and ensuring assessments are evidence-based, appropriately sourced and clearly communicate confidence and uncertainty.
* Identify intelligence gaps and emerging issues requiring additional collection or analytical attention.
* Produce timely written assessments, short-form and longer-form analytical content for senior decision-makers and stakeholders.
* Deliver authoritative briefings to clients and respond confidently to questions from government, defence, security and commercial audiences.
* Build relationships with customers and internal stakeholders, using their intelligence requirements and feedback to help shape research priorities and product development.
* Contribute to the continued development of analytical methodologies, structured analytical techniques and best practices across the Country Intelligence team.

**The ideal skills and experience for this role are:** 

* Specialist expertise relating to Mexico, demonstrated through substantial professional experience researching or working on Mexican political, security, defence, intelligence or organised crime issues.
* Fluent Spanish and English, including the ability to conduct advanced research using Spanish-language primary and secondary sources and engage professionally with Spanish-speaking contacts and stakeholders.
* An established and relevant network of contacts in Mexico and/or the wider region, potentially spanning government, security, defence, academia, journalism, civil society and specialist research communities.
* Detailed knowledge of Mexican NSAGs, cartels and serious and organised crime, including their organisational structures, leadership, geographic presence, capabilities, revenue streams, alliances and competition.
* Strong knowledge of wider Latin American security, political and geopolitical dynamics and an ability to place developments in Mexico within their regional and international context.
* Considerable proven experience in a comparable intelligence, defence, national security, political risk, geopolitical analysis or specialist research role.
* Proven experience leading analysts or researchers, setting priorities, managing workflows and developing colleagues.
* Excellent OSINT collection and analytical skills, with the ability to identify, validate and interpret information from complex and sometimes contradictory source environments.
* Strong source evaluation skills and an understanding of the particular challenges associated with researching organised crime and security issues in Mexico.
* Proven experience in intelligence assessment, risk assessment, scenario analysis and the production of concise, decision-relevant intelligence reporting.
* Strong critical-thinking skills and the ability to distinguish reporting from assessment, identify intelligence gaps, challenge assumptions and communicate analytical confidence and uncertainty.
* Excellent briefing and presentation skills, with demonstrable experience communicating complex intelligence assessments to senior audiences and responding authoritatively to questions.
* Excellent written English, editorial judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to review and improve the analytical work of others.
* Strong stakeholder and client-management skills and the confidence to represent Janes externally as a senior subject-matter expert.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality intelligence content to deadline.
* Strong data analysis skills together with advanced online and electronic research capabilities.

* Leave- study/ volunteer/ reserve forces

* Private medical insurance – BUPA
* Maternity (100% of basic salary for the first 26 weeks followed by Statutory Maternity Pay)
* Paternity (100% of basic salary for 6 weeks)
* Life cover
* Access to LinkedIn Learning
* Access to an on-site gym

# AI Adoption Partner

The AI Adoption Partner is a hands-on AI delivery role where progress is measured in hours and days, not months and years. Our AI is delivered through a defined, sanctioned toolset and inside a clear governance envelope, not through open experimentation with whatever tool is fastest to hand.

Embedded in the business rather than in IT, each AI Adoption Partner finds where AI genuinely moves the needle for their cluster, builds it using internal and external tools and makes sure it is adopted, measured and where it works, spread to the rest of the Group.

The role has three equally weighted objectives: make K3 more efficient; create new or better value for clients; and improve colleagues' working lives by removing repetitive, low-value work. It sits at the intersection of three things that must move together - the Group AI & Data Strategy, the pace the business wants to move at and the obligations (cyber, data and regulatory) K3 already carries as a professional services group.

**Why this role is different**

This is a live build role inside a Group that has already done the strategic groundwork: an approved AI assistant (Aimee), an approved no-code build environment (Claude Artifacts), a Group AI & Data Strategy and a Cyber Security Strategy already in flight. The AI Adoption Partner does not start from a blank page, they start from a governed platform and a live strategic portfolio, and their job is to turn that into delivered, measured value inside their cluster.

Success is tangible and is tracked centrally: time released, stronger client outcomes, new revenue, reduced risk, and a measurably better colleague experience.

**Operating boundaries — what “responsible and fast” means here**

Speed in this role comes from working inside a known toolset and a known governance model, not around one. Every AI Adoption Partner works within:

* Approved toolset only: Aimee and Claude Artifacts. No shadow AI, personal AI accounts, or unapproved frontier-model access.
* K3's AI Policy and “Golden Rule,” data protection obligations and professional / client confidentiality duties, applied from the first prototype not at go-live.
* EU AI Act obligations relevant to K3's dual provider / deployer status, including mandatory risk-tiering of any new use case before it touches live client or candidate data.
* Cost governance: all model usage routed and monitored under the Group's model-routing policy.

**Person specification**

Essential

* Proven use of AI and generative AI to deliver measurable business outcomes, ideally including a named conversational AI assistant and a no-code AI build tool (e.g. a Copilot-class assistant, Claude Artifacts/similar).
* End-to-end delivery experience: problem definition, prototyping, rollout and adoption.
* Able to understand a business problem quickly and turn it into a working solution at pace, inside a defined toolset.
* Sound working knowledge of data protection, client confidentiality and responsible AI in a professional or regulated environment; able to apply a risk-tiering process without being told each time.
* Clear communicator, credible with partners, fee-earners and support teams alike.
* Curious and adaptable, willing to challenge established ways of working while maintaining trust, professional judgement and toolset discipline.

Desirable

* Professional services or regulated-advisory experience.
* Change, product, process-mapping or lean delivery experience.

Location:

Day rate contract, or a fixed-term appointment on LCMB’s payroll. Terms will be agreed with the successful candidate.

About:

LCMB Building Performance Ltd is a specialist building performance consultancy. We advise organisations in higher education, healthcare, commercial property and the public sector on estates strategy, facilities management, compliance, energy and net zero delivery, and major capital programmes. Our work is data-led and focused on measurable outcomes: safer, more reliable, more efficient buildings.

We are a small, experienced team based in Oxfordshire, working with high-profile clients across the UK. This role is delivered through LCMB on behalf of our client.

Role:

LCMB is seeking an experienced Technical Director to support Hard FM operations for one of our Higher Education clients in central London, on an interim basis for six to twelve months.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership role covering a large, complex, multi-site urban campus. You will hold act as the senior technical authority for the executive and academic community, supporting on a number of strategic operational and infrastructure investment projects.

Your work will include:

You will report to a senior member of the client’s estates leadership team, be supported by the LCMB FM operational team and be a visible member of the estates senior management group. The role covers the full strategic operational and infrastructure project across the campus, including:

* Engineering and building services: mechanical, electrical, public health, vertical transportation, BMS and controls, lifts and specialist plant, including laboratory and research environments.
* Utilities and energy: electricity, gas, water, heat networks and standby power, together with resilience planning and energy performance.
* Planned and reactive maintenance, asset management, lifecycle and backlog maintenance planning.
* Statutory and regulatory compliance across the estate, including fire, water hygiene, gas, electrical, asbestos, lifts and pressure systems.
* Minor works and small capital projects delivered through the operations team, technical input to major capital schemes, and the operational interfaces with security, cleaning, grounds and logistics services.

* Provide senior technical and operational leadership, setting priorities and standards for a multi-disciplinary in-house team and outsourced service partners.
* Support statutory compliance and health and safety performance for the operational estate, including governance, reporting, audit response and remediation of findings.
* Manage operational budgets running to several million pounds, including maintenance, utilities and minor works, and drive value for money from contracts and suppliers.
* Guide the management of hard FM and specialist contracts, including performance management, variations and re-procurement where required, and maintain resilience and business continuity for critical infrastructure, including incident response and out-of-hours escalation.
* Provide technical assurance to capital projects and estates strategy, including design reviews, commissioning and handover, and support the client’s carbon reduction and energy performance objectives.
* Build effective working relationships with academic departments, professional services, students’ representatives and external stakeholders, and represent the estates function at senior governance forums.
* Ensure a smooth handover on completion of the assignment, leaving clear documentation, plans and priorities for the permanent post-holder.

About you:

You will be able to demonstrate:

**Essential**

* Substantial senior leadership experience in estates or campus operations for a large, complex organisation, ideally in higher education, healthcare, research or another 24/7 public-facing environment.
* A strong engineering or building services background, with a degree or equivalent and chartered status or equivalent professional standing (for example CIBSE, IET, IMechE, RICS or IWFM).
* Demonstrable ownership of statutory compliance and health and safety across a large estate, with a working knowledge of the relevant UK regulations and guidance.
* Experience managing multi-million-pound operational budgets and large hard FM or engineering contracts.
* Track record of leading in-house teams and outsourced service partners through periods of change.
* Credibility with senior executives and academic stakeholders, with clear, concise written and verbal communication.
* Availability to start within a short notice period and to commit to a six to twelve month assignment.

**Desirable**

* Experience within a university or research-intensive environment, including laboratory and specialist facilities.
* Experience of interim or transition roles, including stabilising teams and handing over to a permanent appointee.
* Knowledge of heat networks, decarbonisation programmes and energy performance in operational estates.
* NEBOSH or equivalent health and safety qualification.

Why this role is different:

Interim technical appointments are often about holding the line until a permanent post-holder arrives. This one is not. You will be the senior technical authority for a central London campus that runs around the clock, spanning research laboratories and specialist plant, heat networks and standby power, and a backlog and lifecycle position with investment decisions attached. You will be expected to make those calls, not set out the options and wait.

The role is also visible. You will sit in the estates senior management group and report to the client’s estates leadership, so you will be in the room when priorities are set and accountable for the technical advice that shapes them. You will work directly with academic departments, professional services and students’ representatives, where problems with the estate are felt daily and reported bluntly.

Unlike most interim appointments, you will not be doing it alone. LCMB’s FM operational team supports the role and provides oversight, giving you specialist input, peer challenge and a second opinion on the difficult judgements. You bring the seniority and take the decisions; we make sure you are not the only person carrying them.

The assignment is also meant to leave something behind. Success is not a stable estate for six to twelve months. It is a clear compliance position, a maintenance and lifecycle plan that stands up to scrutiny, and a successor who inherits an estate in better order than you found it.

Direct applications only – we are not engaging recruitment agencies for this role.
