**About the Team**

  

The Financial Performance & Forecasting (FP&F) function is Finance's forward-looking business partner, responsible for planning, forecasting, performance analysis, executive reporting and decision support. The Europe and Asia Pacific (APAC) FP&F team works closely with Asset Management, Investments, Development, Real Estate Finance, Real Estate Accounting, and Regional Leadership to connect financial and operating performance with the underlying business drivers across Oxford's Europe and APAC portfolios.

  

**Position Summary**

  

The Senior Financial Analyst will support financial planning, forecasting, portfolio performance analysis and executive reporting across Europe and APAC. The role combines strong financial analysis with business partnering and executive storytelling.

  

The successful candidate will contribute to annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, portfolio performance reviews, regional transaction management and regional reporting. The role will also perform scenario modelling,  automation, Power BI & AI-enabled analysis.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

  

**Financial Planning & Forecasting**

·   Support the annual Operating Plan, quarterly forecast and long-range planning processes across Europe and APAC.

·   Coordinate planning inputs with Asset Management (both internal and 3rd party), Investments, Development, Real Estate Finance and other regional stakeholders, helping ensure key assumptions are complete, consistent and supported.

·   Input and consolidate forecast submissions and analyze performance against actual results, prior forecast and Operating Plan.

·   Assess and clearly present the regional outlook, including key risks, opportunities and sensitivities.

·   Analyze key portfolio assumptions, including operating performance, leasing, transactions, deployment, financing, capital expenditure and valuation-related impacts.

·   Build scenario and sensitivity analyses to evaluate changes in business and market conditions.

  

**Performance Reporting & Business Insights**

·   Prepare monthly, quarterly and annual reporting materials for regional leadership, Oxford's Executive Committee, and local Board of Directors.

·   Translate actual and forecast performance into concise, executive-ready insights, presentations, dashboards and written narratives.

·   Analyze investment returns and key performance indicators, including NOI, interest, other gains and losses, capital expenditures, leasing costs, deployment, financing activity and valuation movements.

·   Explain performance across geographies, sectors, investment strategies and assets, distinguishing underlying operating performance from portfolio, transaction and market impacts.

·   Perform return calculations and attribution analysis for pending and completed transactions and support variance analysis against Operating Plan and latest forecast.

·   Support regional P&L and portfolio reviews, highlighting implications, decisions and follow-up actions.

·   Perform quality reviews of reports, presentations and analysis to support accurate, consistent and timely reporting.

  

**Business Partnering & Decision Support**

·   Partner with Asset Management, Investments, Development, Real Estate Finance, Real Estate Accounting, and Regional leadership to develop planning assumptions and performance insights.

·   Support decision-making through scenario analysis, sensitivity modelling, return attribution and business case analysis.

·   Evaluate inputs and challenge assumptions constructively, escalating material inconsistencies, risks and opportunities where appropriate.

·   Translate complex financial and operational information into clear insights and practical recommendations for senior stakeholders.

·   Build effective working relationships across functions, regions and levels of seniority while managing competing priorities in a complex environment.

  

**Transactions & Capital Events**

·   Support and coordinate with Real Estate Accounting and other stakeholders on acquisitions and dispositions.

·   Assist with financial due diligence, transaction impact analysis, agreement review support and the assessment of accounting or reporting implications.

·   Coordinate cross-functional financial support during transaction execution and the onboarding or offboarding of investments.

·   Maintain regional transaction activity data and provide related forecast, return and variance analysis.

  

**Reporting Transformation & Continuous Improvement**

·   Contribute to the evolution of regional Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) capabilities, including driver-based planning, standardized KPIs, scenario modelling and enhanced executive reporting.

·   Support improvements in reporting quality, consistency, timeliness, automation and scalability.

·   Identify opportunities to simplify recurring work, strengthen controls and redirect team capacity toward higher-value analysis.

·   Explore responsible uses of automation and AI-enabled analysis while maintaining appropriate review, data quality and control standards.

·   Complete ad-hoc financial and performance analysis as required.

  

**Required Skills & Experience**

  

**Financial Analysis & Technical Expertise**

·   Three or more years of progressive experience in FP&A, financial analysis, transaction analysis, valuation, audit, or a related field;

·   Strong financial modelling skills and advanced Excel capability.

·   Ability to identify key business drivers, evaluate assumptions and produce forward-looking analysis.

·   Strong PowerPoint capability and the ability to develop clear, executive-ready presentations.

·   Exposure to planning, reporting or consolidation systems; Power BI, data visualization, data transformation, automation or AI-enabled analysis is an asset.

·   Experience in real estate, infrastructure, private markets, alternative investments, multi-currency reporting or a complex organizational environment is an asset.

  

**Communication & Stakeholder Management**

·   Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into concise, decision-ready insights.

·   Ability to collaborate effectively across functions, regions and levels of seniority.

·   Organized, dependable and able to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment.

·   Confidence to ask thoughtful questions and challenge inputs constructively, supported by sound analysis.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

·   Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business or a related discipline.

·   CPA, ACA or equivalent designation, or progress toward completion, is preferred.

  

**Key Competencies**

**Role purpose:**

To provide consultant-level remote clinical input to support timely, safe management of ENT and audiology-related referrals and follow-ups. The post holder will triage referrals, deliver Advice and Guidance (A&G), complete diagnostic reviews (including scans), undertake harm reviews where required, and support delivery of contractual performance requirements (KPIs) while maintaining high standards of clinical governance.

**Key responsibilities:**

• Referral triage (e-RS / SystmOne): clinically triage incoming ENT referrals and associated clinical information to determine urgency, appropriate pathway, investigations required prior to appointment, and most suitable management plan.

• Advice and Guidance (A&G): provide timely, high-quality A&G responses to referring clinicians, including clear recommendations on investigations, interim treatment, red flags, safety-netting, and onward referral where indicated, in line with local pathways and national guidance.

• Contractual KPI delivery: support achievement of contract performance measures (for example response times) by prioritising work appropriately, tracking completion, and escalating capacity or pathway risks early.

• Diagnostic / scan reviews: review relevant investigation results (including imaging and diagnostic reports where provided), document an interpretation within scope, and make clear next-step recommendations (discharge, treatment plan, further investigation, or onward referral).

• Harm reviews: complete harm reviews for patients waiting within the service as required, identifying deterioration, safeguarding concerns, or clinical risk; document outcomes; and ensure appropriate action, escalation, and communication.

• Audiology follow-up: clinically review audiology outcomes and investigations, advise on next steps, and ensure appropriate follow-up plans (including discharge advice, patient-initiated follow-up where appropriate, or onward ENT review).

• Documentation: maintain accurate, timely clinical records on e-RS/SystmOne (or the agreed digital platform), including clear rationale for decisions, coding where required, and completion of mandatory fields needed for reporting and audit.

• Communication: communicate effectively and professionally with referrers, service managers and the wider MDT; provide clear written outputs suitable for sharing with patients/GPs where required.

• Clinical governance: comply with information governance, safeguarding, infection prevention (where relevant to remote work), incident reporting, and participate in audit/quality improvement as agreed.

Clinical Director / Medical Lead (as locally defined).

General Manager / Service Manager, ENT clinicians, audiology team, admin/referral management team, and primary care referrers.

Remote/home working (UK-based), with attendance at virtual virtual doctors meeting as required.

**Systems:**

Access and use of NHS e-Referral Service (e-RS) and SystmOne (or agreed clinical record systems) in line with local information governance requirements.

Turnaround expectations: Deliver A&G and triage activity within agreed service standards and contractual KPIs, escalating promptly where safe turnaround times cannot be met, and supporting the General Manager in maintaining a safe, high-quality service.

• Full registration with the General Medical Council (GMC) with a licence to practise.

• ENT consultant-level experience with ability to provide independent clinical decision-making remotely.

• Demonstrable experience of referral triage and/or delivering specialist Advice and Guidance to primary care (including via NHS e-RS or equivalent).

• Ability to review and interpret investigation results and imaging reports to formulate safe management plans within scope.

• Strong written communication skills, producing clear, actionable clinical advice and safety-netting.

• Competence in using electronic clinical record systems and maintaining high-quality documentation.

• Understanding of clinical governance, incident reporting, safeguarding, confidentiality and information governance.

• Ability to work autonomously, manage workload against turnaround times/KPIs, and escalate risk appropriately.

**Desirable:**

• Prior experience using SystmOne in community services.

• Experience of working within or alongside community/intermediate ENT services and pathways.

• Experience of working closely with audiology services, including review of audiology investigations and follow-up planning.

• Evidence of participation in audit, quality improvement and service development related to outpatient transformation and/or triage.

**Compliance and professional requirements:**

• Maintain appraisal and revalidation in line with GMC requirements.

• Hold appropriate professional indemnity cover for the duties undertaken.

• Enhanced DBS clearance (adult/child workforce) as required by the service.

• Completion of mandatory training (including safeguarding and information governance) in line with organisational policy.

• Adhere to all information governance and data security requirements for remote working (secure workspace, approved devices, secure connectivity).

**Key deliverables:**

• Consistent, high-quality triage outcomes recorded on e-RS/SystmOne, with clear rationale and pathway direction.

• Timely A&G responses meeting agreed turnaround standards and supporting avoidance of unnecessary outpatient activity where clinically appropriate.

• Completed scan/diagnostic reviews with documented clinical plan and appropriate communication to stakeholders.

• Completed harm reviews with actions, escalation and tracking where risk is identified.

• Documented audiology follow-up decisions and outcomes, including onward referral when needed.

Building and maintaining the data processing pipelines that run on our satellites' Nvidia Jetson computers.

Working with our Flight Software, Systems and Operations teams, and with payload partners, to balance mission needs against what the hardware can do.

Strong Python skills for data processing, and clean, testable, maintainable code.
Hands-on experience with embedded Linux and ARM-based hardware.
Experience with GPU computing and performance optimisation, such as CUDA on Nvidia platforms.

Experience turning scientific or analytical code into efficient production software.

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

We’re looking for Sales Development Representative to join our team covering the Nordics region coverage includes Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland.

In this role, you'll help drive Pleo’s growth and be part of the team responsible for expanding our footprint in spend management solutions as we scale our cutting-edge SaaS platform.

**What you’ll be doing**

As a Sales Development Representative you will:

* Build a pipeline through cold calling, social and email outreach to senior finance leaders.
* Qualify potential deals before passing them to Account Executives.
* Nurture relationships with Prospects.
* Use best in class tools for creative prospecting.
* Enable others and share best practices to learn as a team.
* Work towards achieving daily and weekly revenue targets and key performance

**What you bring**

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

* Previous professional experience in a customer-facing or sales-related role (preferably sales, finance, consulting)
* Driven and ambitious individual looking to grow quickly in sales
* Proactive and ready to take on own initiatives to drive results
* Comfortable with cold calling & getting out of your comfort zone
* Thrive on sales targets and constantly seek new ways to go the extra mile where needed
* A team player who goes out of their way to help colleagues succeed
* Entrepreneurial and creative mindset, ready to learn and grow every day
* Thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment and excited to grow alongside the company
* Fluent in **English** (company language) and **Danish or Swedish** (Essential)

**Who you’ll be working with and reporting to**

* You’ll report to our SDR Manager Europe and work closely with our in region Account Executives, as well as our marketing and partnerships teams. Our team of 4 is highly collaborative and dedicated to business growth.

**How you’ll develop in this role**

* In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:
* Lead initiatives to drive impact in expanding Pleo’s presence in the Benelux market.
* Grow your skills in sales and outbound strategies, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale its operations across Benelux.
* We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in sales.

**Show me the benefits!**

* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis
* We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options
* Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Access to LinkedIn Learning - acquire new skills, stay abreast of industry trends and fuel your personal and professional development continuously
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

## **The interview process**

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. An Interview with the Hiring Manager - 45 mins.
3. Our Pleo Challenge - 60 mins - A case study/role play with our panel to demonstrate your ability
4. A bar raiser interview - 30 mins To allow you to showcase what extra value you can add to Pleo's growth journey!

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for SDRs, we received many applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

* CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!
* Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

## **About your application**

* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

## Job Description

The role is the single senior point of accountability that bridges construction, operations and the customer during the build and handover phases. It owns the customer relationship through delivery, protects and grows revenue from customer works, and builds the capability to deliver Pure DC’s own lifecycle capital programmes. Where projects sit outside the UK, the Head of Project Management leverages the regional team and approved third parties to award and manage delivery consistently to Pure DC standards.

**The role is built around three core pillars of responsibility:**

* **1. Construction-to-operations bridge –**Acting as the customer’s relationship manager through the build phase, handling variations and change requests, and ensuring a controlled transition into operations. * **2. Customer growth and additional revenue –**Engaging with customers early enough to identify and win works that would otherwise be lost to third parties – for example white-space cabling, structured cabling and fit-out – intercepting activity ahead of competitors where commercially viable.
* **3. Lifecycle capex delivery –**Building and leading the capability to plan and deliver Pure DC’s own lifecycle capital works, including repair, replacement and end-of-life upgrade programmes as the portfolio scales.

**Strategic customer ownership**

The role provides each key hyperscaler tenant with a consistent, single point of contact across their Pure DC estate – for example acting as the relationship lead for key clients across EMEA – and coordinating with the regional team to maintain equivalent ownership for customers across the Middle East and Asia.

The Head of Project Management must carry out the following diligently, following industry guidelines and best-practice techniques:

* Apply value engineering to reduce cost through creative solutions with no impact on quality or reliability.

**Lifecycle & internal projects**

* Support and, where complexity requires, lead site engineering teams on in-house operational projects – e.g. office/space redesign, end-of-life-cycle replacements and building H&S upgrades.
* Anticipate, plan and deliver lifecycle capital replacement programmes across the portfolio.

**Leadership**

* Lead and develop the project delivery function, including line management of the Regional Project Manager (Middle East & Asia) and coordination of third-party delivery partners.

## Description

**About us**

Qureight’s mission is to accelerate clinical trials and ensure breakthroughs in lung and heart disease reach patients without delay. Our AI-powered data and imaging curation platform enables the analysis of clinical imaging and other healthcare data, helping our customers bring treatments to market, faster.

We’re looking for talented people who want their work to matter. With offices in Cambridge and London, you’ll join our multidisciplinary team of clinicians, scientists, and engineers. What unites us is our open culture, continuous learning mindset, and a shared mission to help biopharma run faster, smarter trials.

**About the role**

We are looking for a technically-minded Product Owner to support the development of Qureight’s imaging platform that orchestrates complex workflows across a growing number of global trial sites and studies. The imaging platform supports two major customers. Firstly, our internal Clinical Operations team use the platform and its admin tooling to manage users, sites, and project onboarding. Secondly, our external clinical trial site users and pharmaceutical sponsors access different products hosted on the platform. The Product Owner will own agile delivery for the Platform team: taking the requirements, priorities and roadmap set by the Head of Product Management and turning them into well-defined, technically sound work the team can build.

The Head of Product Management owns the product roadmap, prioritisation, and all direct engagement with Clinical Operations, site users and sponsors. Your role picks up from there: translating agreed requirements into technical and architectural decisions, breaking them into implementation-ready user stories and tasks, and running the Platform team's day-to-day agile process (sprint planning, refinement, and review) so that what gets built matches both the customer requirement and represents sound engineering practice. Product Owners at Qureight tend to be technical by background, often coming from a development role, since a large part of this job is working directly alongside engineers on the implementation approach, not just defining what to build.

**What you will do**

The Product Owner will provide outstanding product ownership and requirements management for the Platform team, including:

* **Agile delivery ownership.** Run the Platform team's day-to-day agile process (sprint planning, backlog refinement, and prioritisation within the sprint), turning requirements and priorities set by the Head of Product Management into a well-organised, appropriately-sized backlog.
* **Requirements translation.** Take user requirements and priorities defined by the Head of Product Management and translate them into clear technical and architectural decisions the Platform team can build against.
* **Story & task breakdown.** Break requirements down into implementation-ready user stories and technical tasks, working directly with engineers on approach and sequencing.
* **Acceptance criteria & test specs.** Define acceptance criteria and test specifications for backlog items, and validate delivered work against them before it reaches users.
* **Engineering partnership.** Work embedded within the Platform team through planning, refinement, and review ceremonies, effectively part of the engineering team from a process and delivery perspective.
* **UX input.** Bring a UX-informed perspective to feature design and prioritisation, especially for the products that external site users and sponsors interact with directly (e.g. Central Read system, upload UI, and sponsor dashboard), as well as the Clinical Operations admin tooling.
* **Technical input upward.** Act as the Platform team's main point of contact for the Head of Product Management, surfacing technical constraints, feasibility, and delivery risk that should inform prioritisation and roadmap decisions.
* **GxP-aware delivery.** Ensure requirements and backlog items affecting GxP-relevant systems are documented and validated in line with Qureight's ISMS and Management of Software Policy.

## Requirements

**What we need**

 To thrive in this role, you'll need:

* Previous experience as a Product Owner, or as a developer/engineer moving into a product ownership or delivery-focused role, working directly within an engineering team.
* Solid hands-on experience with Agile ways of working, including running sprint planning, refinement, and retrospectives.
* Strong JIRA skills, with proven experience structuring and managing epics and backlogs.
* Comfortable engaging in technical and architectural discussions, and translating requirements into implementation-ready stories and tasks.
* Ability to write clear acceptance criteria and test specifications.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfortable working between technical teams and Product stakeholders.
* Comfortable managing a backlog and delivery cadence in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment.
* Some UX experience (e.g. usability testing, wireframing), useful when translating requirements into implementation but not core to the role.
* Experience working on products used in clinical trials, healthcare, or another regulated environment.
* Familiarity with GxP, ISO 27001, or computerised system validation (CSV) concepts.

**Even better if**

* A software engineering or development background, or other hands-on technical experience.

## Benefits

**What can you expect from us**

* A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, cycle-to-work scheme, and a contributory pension scheme
* Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Qureight

* **28 days’ holiday allowance**, 25 days’ annual leave and 3 additional company days between Christmas and New Year, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave

* A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields, including software engineering, DevOps, data science, machine learning, quality assurance, regulatory affairs, and clinical operations.

**How to apply**

Please upload a CV and covering letter by clicking 'Apply Now'. Your covering letter should explain why you are applying for the job and what skills and experience you can bring to the role.

We review CVs as we receive them and interview as soon as we have applications that look like a good match (usually within one week). We do not use closing dates. So, please apply as soon as possible to avoid missing out on this role. We advertised this role on Monday 28th September 2026.

If you have any queries, please contact careers@qureight.com.

Your primary role is to ensure that the writing of new packaging material specifications/ packaging assembly specifications/ finished goods specifications and the revision of existing ones is done so following the Business Process defined by Business Process Leader- Packaging Materials and in the process raise the quality of packaging material specifications to that defined in the data quality standard for the commodities which are in your portfolio. * Help transform our packaging material specification portfolio with focus on the assigned Packaging commodities.

* Good communication, influencing and interpersonal skills with the ability to operate successfully in various team capacities, a multi-cultural environment, at senior levels and with external partners.

* Ability to effectively prioritise and execute tasks under pressure.
* Strong commercial awareness and understanding of corporate codes of conduct.
* Willingness to improve understanding of the product lifecycle and of regulations impacting the FMCG sector.

# Director of People

As our Director of People, you will help define that future. You will create an environment where people can thrive, leaders bring out the best in their teams, and our values are felt in everyday decisions. You will have the influence to make Redsquid a place where exceptional people choose to join, grow and stay – a place they’ll describe as the most loved.

## What you'll own

**The best place to work, made real.**

Own the engagement agenda end to end — what we measure, what it tells us, and what changes as a result. Hold the group to its B Corp and Best Companies standards and use them as a management discipline rather than an accreditation exercise. Be the person who notices when the stated culture and the lived experience have drifted apart, and who does something about it. 

**People operations and employee relations.**

A People function that is accurate, fast and trusted: contracts, policy, HRIS, payroll interface, absence, performance and casework. Sixteen acquired businesses means legacy terms, inherited practices and inconsistent data — bring that onto one credible platform without stripping out what made each business good. Handle complex ER and TUPE matters yourself, with sound judgement on risk. 

**Talent acquisition.**

Own how we attract and hire, in-house wherever possible. Build the employer brand that our B Corp status, share scheme and growth story already justify, reduce reliance on agencies, and hold a quality bar that leaders respect. Hiring at pace in a competitive MSSP/MSP market is a commercial capability, not a support service. 

**Learning, development and career pathways.**

Every colleague should be able to see a route forward and know what it takes to get there. Own the progression frameworks, the technical and commercial development offer, and the group’s management capability programme — because the single biggest driver of whether someone thrives here is the quality of their line manager. Partner with the Director of Education so the group’s learning assets work for our own people as well as our customers. 

**The people side of M&A — owned, not delivered.**

The M&A people partner in your team runs the day-to-day integration work: diligence input, TUPE and harmonisation, day-one experience, post-acquisition engagement. You own the standard they work to, the playbook they use and the outcome the group gets — retention of key talent, integration pace, and an honest read on which of the previous eleven integrations worked and which did not. You step in personally on the complex and the contentious, and you are the one accountable to the Executive team for people risk in any deal. 

**Organisation design and leadership capability.**

Work with the Group MD on the shape of the group as it scales — structure, spans, succession and the leadership bench. Bring rigour to how we assess and develop senior people, building on the Lumina and leadership assessment work already in use. 

**Reward and recognition.**

A reward architecture that is defensible across sixteen businesses and legible to colleagues: pay frameworks, benchmarking, the EMI scheme narrative, recognition, and sales incentive design in partnership with the commercial and finance leadership. 

**People data the board can act on.**

Own the people metrics in the group KPI framework — retention, regrettable attrition, time to hire, cost per hire, engagement, manager effectiveness, absence — and present them to the Executive team and board with a clear view of what they mean commercially and what you intend to do about them.

## What success looks like

|  |  |
| --- | --- |

You can describe, with evidence, where the employee experience is strongest and where it is failing. The People team knows what you expect of them. You have a clear read on ER risk, data quality and the state of the last three integrations, and you have brought the Executive team an honest diagnosis rather than a plan. |
| **First 6 months** | A people plan agreed with the Executive team and landed with the SLT, with named priorities and measures that sit inside the group KPI framework. People operations running cleanly and consistently across the group. The manager capability programme designed and started. Talent acquisition in hand, with an agency spend trajectory you can defend. You are the person leaders call before they call a lawyer. |
| **First 12 months** | Engagement and retention measurably improved and attributable to specific things you changed. Career pathways published and in use. A repeatable people integration playbook, proven on a live acquisition. B Corp recertification requirements on track for 2027. Colleagues describing Redsquid as a place where they can build a career — and our hiring pipeline reflecting that. |

## Who you are

**Essential** 

* Senior generalist People leadership in a multi-site, multi-entity business — ideally in a people-and-skills business where talent is the product.

* Direct experience of M&A from the people side: diligence, TUPE, harmonisation and post-deal integration. You have done this more than once and can say what you would do differently.

* Commercially literate and commercially credible. You can hold your own on a P&L, connect people decisions to margin, retention and delivery capacity, and be challenged by a CFO without retreating.

React Front End Developer required to join our Satalia team in UK
As an organisation, we push the boundaries of data science, optimisation and artificial intelligence to solve the most complex problems in the industry. Satalia, a WPP company is a community of individuals devoted to working on diverse and challenging projects, allowing you to flex your technical skills whilst working with a tight-knit team of high performing colleagues.
Led by our founder and WPP Chief AI Officer Daniel Hulme, Satalia's ambition is to become a decentralised organisation of the future. Today, this involves developing tools and processes to liberate and automate manual repetitive tasks, with a focus on freedom, transparency and trust. At the core of our thinking is an approach to wellbeing and inclusivity. We unpack human behaviour and unpick prejudice to ensure a safe and inviting environment. We offer truly flexible working and allow our employees to find the working practice that makes them most productive. At Satalia, your opinion matters and your achievements are celebrated.
What you'll be doing
Solve is a shared visual workspace where people and AI agents work on the same problem together. People define the problem, bring the context and steer the work. Agents research, plan and deliver. The work and the reasoning behind it stay on the board, visible to everyone.
The board is a real-time collaborative canvas, and it is the product. We are hiring a senior frontend engineer to build it with us. This is hands-on work on hard, concrete frontend problems: direct manipulation, streaming AI output, and several people editing the same board at once. Not a chat window around an API.
You will spend most of your time shipping code in the canvas and collaboration layer, working closely with the technical lead, who sets direction. We want your advice on how things should be built, and we will take it. We are not asking you to run a roadmap or a team.
Small senior team: technical lead, architect, QA, and you. Internal alpha today, funded, with a path to becoming its own venture. React and TypeScript frontend, Python and FastAPI behind it. Agents do a lot of the delivery work; people own the judgement. We prototype to learn, keep systems simple and legible, and treat specs, designs and tests as part of the product.
The project is a real-time collaborative canvas, and it is the product. We are hiring a senior frontend engineer to build it with us. This is hands-on work on hard, concrete frontend problems: direct manipulation, streaming AI output, and several people editing the same board at once. Not a chat window around an API.
You will work on:
The canvas: pan, zoom, drag, selection, spatial layout, rich interactive cards, and keeping all of it fast with hundreds of cards live.
Frontend state across transient interaction, persistent product state and server-authoritative data.
Real-time collaboration: presence, optimistic updates, reconnects, missed-event recovery and conflict handling.
Real-time event handling: the canvas event stream runs on Server-Sent Events today (EventSource, heartbeats, token-authenticated streams, backoff reconnects). You will own the client side of it, and help decide where WebSockets would earn their place.
AI-facing surfaces: streaming output, agent status, partial results, approvals and recovery.
Performance, accessibility and test strategy for all of the above.

Your first body of work is already defined. Two or more people, and the agents working for them, edit the same canvas at once and nobody loses work. No fork banner, no silent drop, no whole-board repaint. The design is decided and about 40% of the cards are done. What remains is the client side of it: the per-entity patch wire over the SSE stream, optimistic apply with resync on a missed event, the pending-edits queue that survives a reload, and closing out the remaining data-loss defects on the load, save-conflict and live-update paths. The interview questions come from this work.
What we want from you
We are not looking for someone who ticks every box. We are looking for someone who understands the core technology well, and who we would enjoy working with. In order of weight:
Deep React (or equivalent) and browser-state expertise. This is the gate. You can explain how you reason about state ownership, rendering and browser performance, component decomposition, and interactions that fail part way through. You diagnose before you prescribe.
You have built a complex interactive product. A canvas, editor, map, design tool, whiteboard or collaborative app, and you can connect the technical decisions to what users did as a result. You understand that collaborative software needs explicit rules for authority and conflict. You have shipped real-time event handling over WebSockets or Server-Sent Events, and can explain ordering, reconnects and missed-event recovery on an unreliable connection.
AI-native curiosity. You use coding agents seriously, know where they help and where they bite, and you are interested in the frontend problems AI products create: streaming, long-running work, trust and control. This is the one area where curiosity substitutes for experience.
You are comfortable across the API boundary: you can design a request and response shape with the backend, reason about idempotency and optimistic concurrency, and decide which side owns a given piece of state.
Monorepos, CI, quality gates, feature flags and design systems are useful supporting evidence. They are not the centre of this role.

Satalia is home to some of the brightest minds in AI and if you're looking to join a company who not only values autonomy and freedom, but embraces a culture of inclusion and warmth, we'd love to hear from you.
We aim to respond to all applications within 2 weeks. If you have not heard from us within 2 weeks this means your application has been unsuccessful.
By applying to Satalia you are expressly giving your consent for the collection and use of your information as described within our Satalia Recruitment Privacy Policy.
Good luck!

SZC’s business is to design, finance, construct, commission, operate, maintain, and eventually decommission the nuclear power plant and related infrastructure (including activities relating to hydrogen, direct air capture and/or desalination) at Sizewell C in Suffolk. The principal objectives of the current development phase of the SZC project are to agree and implement the Capital Raise Plan, including completing an equity and debt raise, agree the core supply chain contracts and obtain the regulatory permits and licences required for the construction phase of the Project (including the core environmental permits and nuclear site licence). 

 

Prior to the government investment decision SZC operated as part of EDF in the Nuclear Development business unit and was staffed by EDF colleagues and independent contractors who are now in the process of transferring to the direct employment of SZC.  It is setting itself up as an organisation capable of delivering a new nuclear power plant, from investment case and funding, to construction, commissioning, operations, maintenance and decommissioning.   

 

The SZC construction programme has a technical and commercial business case predicated on technical replication of Hinkley Point C.  EDF will be an important supplier of nuclear capability for the SZC Programme from its established nuclear business footprint in the UK.

# Senior Software Engineer – Front-End

Cambridge, England, United Kingdom

At Speechmatics, we’re expanding our user platform offering. We're looking for a Senior Front-End Software Engineer with a strong product mindset to help drive that growth. This is an opportunity to own end-to-end feature development at a leading-edge AI company, from shaping the user experience through to shipping and iterating based on real user feedback and analytics data.

**What you'll do**

* Own product features from ideation through to delivery, contributing to UX thinking, frontend execution, and post-launch iteration
* Build polished, accessible user interfaces using React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS
* Make UX and UI decisions independently, collaborating closely with designers and PMs rather than waiting on detailed handoffs
* Design and run A/B tests to validate product decisions and surface insights that improve the user experience
* Use analytics tooling such as Mixpanel to understand how people interact with the product and feed that learning back into what gets built
* Partner with backend engineers, product managers, and designers to ship features that genuinely move the needle for users and the business
* Write and maintain robust UI tests, taking ownership of quality in production and at scale
* Run user interviews and meet customers to understand how people use the product and what drives adoption

**What you'll need**

* Proficiency in React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS with a track record of shipping production-quality frontend code
* A product-minded engineering approach
* Comfort owning UX and UI decisions independently
* Hands-on experience with iterative development practices, including A/B testing and feature experimentation
* Familiarity with user analytics tools such as Mixpanel or a comparable platform
* Experience with UI testing frameworks and a solid grounding in frontend engineering best practices
* Confidence collaborating cross-functionally with designers, PMs, and backend engineers
* A track record of using user feedback and data to improve features

**Nice to have**

* Experience using coding agents (eg Claude, Codex, OpenCode) to improve productivity and code quality
* Exposure to backend development, including RESTful APIs and cloud deployments
* Experience conducting or participating in user interviews as part of a product discovery process

*We encourage you to apply even if you do not feel you match all of the requirements exactly. The list of requirements is intended to show the kinds of experience and qualities we’re looking for, but it is not exhaustive. If you are interested in the role, the team, and our mission, we would love to consider your application. We are always open to conversations and look forward to hearing from you.*

**Who we are:**

Speechmatics is the leading expert in Speech Intelligence, and uses AI and Machine Learning to unlock business value in human speech worldwide. We work with an amazing mix of global companies, and our technology can integrate into our customers stack irrespective of their industry or use case – making it the go-to solution to harness useful information from speech.

Joining us means working with some of the smartest minds around the world, focused on cutting-edge projects and deploying the latest techniques to disrupt the market. We believe in putting people first; we’ll do all we can to help you develop your skills and give you the tools you need to thrive. Our Focus Fridays give you an undisturbed day of focus, offset with Together Tuesdays when we have our team meetings, so you've always got the right balance.

We have structured a hybrid approach that includes 2-3 designated office days each week. This arrangement ensures that while we embrace the advantages of remote work, we also maintain the vital connection and synergy that only in-person interactions can foster.

This is only the beginning; we’re looking for amazing people like you to continue our journey...

**What we can offer you:**

No matter what stage of your career you’re at - from paid internships and first-job opportunities through to management and senior positions - we’ll support you with the training and development needed to reach your career aspirations with us. There really is no shortage of opportunities here for you to get involved and collaborate with those around you to deliver your best work.

We offer incredibly flexible working, regular company lunches, and birthday celebrations. But that’s not all. We’ve spoken to our teams to find out what they want. From Private Medical, and Dental for you and your family, through to global working opportunities, a generous holiday allowance and pension/401K matching, we want to make sure our employees and their families are looked after. Every employee will receive a working from home allowance for tech or home office equipment (on top of your choice of laptop and accessories of course). Our approach to parental leave is designed to support employees globally. While this varies by geo, we have support in place for parents (including adoption assistance and reproductive health services) to ensure they have the time and financial resources needed to care for their growing families.

**At Speechmatics, our mission is simple: Understand Every Voice out there.**

That's not just about our tech – it's the heart and soul of who we are. We welcome different experiences, viewpoints, and identities. For us, it’s not just the right thing to do; it’s our catalyst for sparking innovation and creativity. Our teams thrive in an environment that celebrates and supports everyone – no matter their gender, identity or expression, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion, belief, marital status, national origin, veteran status, pregnancy, or maternity status.

But we don’t just open the door to diversity – we actively welcome it. Why? Because we believe every unique voice adds something special to our team, leading us to smarter solutions and a better workplace.

**So, come as you are and join our Speechling community.** We’re building a place where every voice not only gets heard but is also respected and valued.

For more information on us,please visit our website and follow Speechmatics on our social channels via Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube.

# Customer Success Manager - UK Market

**Help UK businesses transform the way they manage company spend**

At Spendesk, we help businesses take control of their spending through a powerful all-in-one platform for company cards, expenses, invoices, procurement and financial workflows.

As a **Customer Success Manager**, you will be the trusted partner of our UK customers. You will help Finance teams get measurable value from Spendesk, drive long-term product adoption and build strong partnerships with the people responsible for managing company spend.

This is **not a support role**. You will own a portfolio of mid-market customers, understand their business priorities, anticipate risks, support renewals and identify opportunities to help them get even more value from Spendesk.

You will work closely with Account Managers, Product, Marketing and Support to deliver an outstanding customer experience and make the voice of our UK customers heard across the company.

**This role is based in the UK. Professional proficiency in English is an essential requirement for the position.**

**What you’ll do**

**Build trusted customer relationships**

* Manage a portfolio of approximately **120 to 150 UK mid-market customers**.
* Build strong relationships with Finance Managers, CFOs, Finance Directors and other key decision-makers.
* Understand each customer’s business priorities, challenges and definition of success.
* Advise customers on best practices and help them optimise their use of Spendesk.
* Lead regular account reviews and develop success plans aligned with customer objectives.
* Become a trusted advisor throughout the customer lifecycle.

**Drive adoption, value and retention**

* Guide customers through onboarding and ensure a smooth transition into long-term adoption.
* Monitor account health, product usage and engagement levels.
* Identify risks early and take proactive action to prevent churn.
* Help customers measure and communicate the business value and ROI of Spendesk.
* Support customers through organisational changes, new stakeholders and evolving business needs.
* Ensure customers continuously discover and adopt relevant Spendesk features.

**Contribute to customer growth**

* Identify relevant upsell and cross-sell opportunities based on customer needs, usage and business context.
* Partner closely with Account Managers to develop and convert expansion opportunities.
* Support renewal discussions by ensuring customers clearly understand the value they receive.
* Contribute to portfolio growth while maintaining a strong customer-first approach.

**Represent the voice of the customer**

* Share structured and actionable customer feedback with Product, Marketing and Sales.
* Identify recurring customer needs, friction points and potential product improvements.
* Support the launch and adoption of new features in the UK market.
* Contribute to customer advocacy initiatives, including testimonials, referrals and case studies.
* Help internal teams better understand the needs of UK Finance teams.

**What we’re looking for**

**Must-have experience and skills**

* **Professional working proficiency in English is essential for this role.**
* Previous experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Client Management or another customer-facing role.
* A consultative approach: you proactively advise customers rather than simply react to requests.
* Strong ownership and autonomy in managing a customer portfolio.
* The ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders.
* An analytical mindset, with the ability to use customer data to identify risks and opportunities.
* Excellent communication, organisation and stakeholder management skills.
* A genuine interest in customer experience, SaaS and building long-term customer partnerships.
* The ability to manage priorities effectively across a high-volume portfolio.

**Strong pluses**

* Experience in SaaS, fintech, payments, accounting, ERP or financial software.
* Experience working with Finance, Accounting or Operations teams.
* Experience managing a mid-market customer portfolio at scale.
* Experience with onboarding, adoption, retention, renewals or expansion.
* Familiarity with tools such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Gainsight, Planhat, Intercom or similar platforms.
* Experience working in a Customer Success and Account Management model.

As we are an international team, please submit your application and CV in English.

**About Spendesk**   
Spendesk is the AI-powered spend management and procurement platform that transforms company spending. By simplifying procurement, payment cards, expense management, invoice processing, and accounting automation, Spendesk sets the new standard for spending at work. Its single, intelligent solution makes efficient spending easy for employees and gives finance leaders the full visibility and control they need across all company spend, even in multi-entity structures. Trusted by thousands of companies, Spendesk supports over 200,000 users across brands such as Payfit, Accor, Welcome to the Jungle, Swile, Big Mamma, Malt and Yousign. With offices in the United Kingdom, France, Spain and Germany, Spendesk also puts community at the heart of its mission.

Spendeskers come from all over the world (35+ countries and counting!) but we have plenty in common: we're bold, ever-curious, committed to kindness, and tackle every challenge with a positive mindset.  **About our benefits**

## **Director of Product, Workflows**

CreatorIQ is the software enterprise brands and agencies run their creator marketing programs on. A large customer works with thousands of creators a year across dozens of programs and several markets, and every one of those partnerships has to be sourced, vetted, agreed, briefed, tracked and paid for. You'll own that operational core and lead the product teams that cover it today, accountable for making the whole thing feel like one operation instead of a series of handoffs.

The mandate is to rebuild that operation around AI. Tooling in this category, ours included, was designed for a world where a person did each step by hand, and it still assumes that. It scales by adding people. A community manager keeping a 2,000-creator program on track lives in spreadsheets. An agency casting 300 creators against a brief in a week gets there by throwing bodies at it. Your job is to change what the software is responsible for, so programs scale without the headcount and the people running them spend their time on decisions that need judgment.

**In this role, you’ll get to:**

* Own the workflow end to end. Discovery, Lists, Community, Campaigns and Messaging are one continuous job for our customers, and today they feel like separate products. Making them one, and making most of it happen without a human clicking through it, is the mandate.
* Lead and grow a team of product managers. You'll set the bar for how they work, coach them on discovery and judgment, and give them enough room to own their surfaces without you in the middle of every decision.
* Decide what gets rebuilt agentically, what gets simplified, and what gets deleted. Plenty of our existing workflow exists because someone needed a manual solution in 2020. Some of it should be automated, some should be replaced by a better model of the problem, and some should just go away.
* Get the trust model right. Provenance, confidence, human-in-the-loop review, honest failure, and clean rollback are what decide whether an enterprise customer lets an agent touch a live campaign.
* Partner with engineering and design leadership on architecture and delivery. Schema, core service, bulk operations, permissions, the data model that both the UI and the agents read from. You need to be credible in those conversations, not just present for them.

**Who you are and what you’ll need for this position:**

* You've spent 8+ years in product, including 2+ leading product managers. Titles matter less than the work, but we need someone who has managed PMs before and knows the difference between coaching and taking over.
* You've owned a broad, workflow-heavy B2B SaaS surface where the product is the customer's daily job.
* You have a builder's mindset and haven't stopped being hands-on. You prototype. You use AI tools to build the thing rather than write a doc about the thing, and you expect the same from your team.
* You've rebuilt a manual workflow around AI and know the difference between removing the work and putting a chat box in front of the same twelve clicks. You're fluent in the mechanics too: retrieval, tool use, evaluation, human-in-the-loop review, and where an agent shouldn't be allowed to act alone.
* You have real product taste and you use it on AI output. You can look at an agent's plan, a generated brief, or a search result and say why it's good or why it's plausible-sounding filler. You ask the same question of a big customer's request or an inherited roadmap item: does this actually solve the problem?
* You're technical enough to hold your own on data model and API design. Schemas, CRUDL, bulk operations, permissions, third-party integrations. You can tell when a small-sounding request is touching something structural.
* You can prioritize across teams with genuinely competing claims and explain the tradeoff so the people who lost the argument still understand it.
* You write well. Most of how we work is async and in docs, and a Director who can only communicate in meetings will not scale here.
* You take initiative and own outcomes. You don't wait to be told the priority, and you'd rather bring a proposal than a list of questions. You're curious, self-driven, low-ego, and allergic to "that's not my job."

We're Stream, the world's first social impact unicorn.
More than four million workers use Stream to get a fairer deal with their money. We reach them through 2,000+ employers, including Greene King, Bupa, Burger King, Asda and the NHS, and it all runs through one simple app where people can earn, learn, save, spend and borrow on terms that actually suit them.
We're VC-backed, growing fast and making waves with our financial wellbeing products. We operate under a social charter that holds us accountable: every product we create has to measurably improve financial wellbeing. Moving money for millions of people, at pace, leaves no room for getting it wrong. That's what makes the work worth doing.
Why this role is different:
The agent types; you decide. Every engineer gets company-paid Claude Code, and agents write most of our code. There are usage caps, but they're guardrails rather than limits: hit one and we'll raise it. Typing time has gone down and decision density has gone up. So we hire for judgement: what to build, what to cut, when to step in and when to let the agent run. You own every line that ships.
A small team with a big footprint. Around 45 people across product and engineering, in small cross-functional pods, serving millions of people in the UK and US. Your work is visible, and it matters.
Engineers pitch the work. Anyone, at any level, can write an RFC, and good ones get built: our engineers wrote more than 30 in August and September alone. In January one of our engineers proposed connecting our Figma design system to Claude Code, so agents build screens from our real components instead of guessing. Two months later it was live in the UK app.
What you'll work on:
The team you join depends on your experience and where you'll have the most impact. Most of the work is making proven products better for millions of people. Some of it is greenfield.
FlexPay: our earned wage access product in the UK and US. Simple, trusted experiences built on payroll integrations and money-moving services at scale.
Credit: responsible workplace loans, covering eligibility, decisioning, servicing and repayment, with real regulatory rigour. Live in the UK and expanding in the US.
Wealth: our emerging workplace savings product. It's early-stage, with plenty of room to shape it.
Benefits & Discounts: helping employees' money go further through benefits and everyday savings, powered by partner integrations.
Integrations: working with our Delivery team to connect new employers' payroll and workforce systems so they can launch on Stream.
Internal tools: the tools that help Stream teams give clients and their employees a better experience.
Two of the hard problems you'd be working on:
Payroll data from dozens of providers. Every employer runs pay differently: Workday, Zellis, ADP, Sage, Fourth, even servers in a customer's own building. We turn all of it into an accurate, up-to-date figure for what each person has earned, because that figure is what they can draw.
Money across rails. Faster Payments, SEPA and US payment rails, direct debits and card repayments, across several banking providers. When a bank's API times out, the payment may still have gone through; retry blindly and someone gets paid twice. Every penny has to reconcile.
How we work:
Value, Speed, Simplicity, in that order. Everything we build is tied to a real user need. We prefer short feedback loops to polished first attempts. We build the smallest thing that works.
Stack: Python (Flask), Postgres, Celery and AWS (ECS, Lambda, SQS) on the backend; React and TypeScript across web and mobile; GitHub Actions for CI/CD. Experience with our stack helps, but isn't required.
Cross-functional by default. You'll work day to day with product, design, data, delivery and commercial colleagues, not from a ticket queue.
What success looks like:
By month 1: you've shipped your first change to production, met your team and the people you'll work with across the business, and understand how money moves through our platform.
By month 3: you're owning problems from discovery to production, whether that's an employee-facing feature, a new employer integration or an internal tool. You've pitched at least one idea of your own.
By month 6: you own a significant area. As a Senior, you're raising the quality bar in your pod. As a Lead, you're also setting technical direction across a wider area and helping other engineers do their best work.
What we're looking for:
A track record of building and running customer-facing software in production, whether web, mobile or backend services and integrations.
Sound judgement: you can turn an ambiguous problem into the simplest thing that works, and explain what you chose not to build.
Experience with, or real curiosity about, working with AI coding agents: directing them, checking their output and knowing when to take over.
Care for reliability, security and data protection. This is people's money.
For Lead: you've set technical direction across more than one team or system, and made the engineers around you better.

It takes about three weeks from application to offer.
Initial call: a short chat about you, the role and what you're looking for.
Technical discovery: a conversation about your experience, your technical knowledge and the things you build for fun.
Live build: a 60-minute screen-shared session where you build with your own AI tools and your preferred stack. There's no take-home and no prep; we share the brief on the call.

At **Style Acre**, technology isn’t just about computers and systems – it can help people live more independently, stay connected, and have greater choice and control in their lives.

You’ll be responsible for the day-to-day management and development of Style Acre’s IT and technology, including:

* Managing the supply, installation, maintenance and repair of IT equipment, including laptops, desktops, servers, tablets and mobile phones.
* Supporting CCTV, home automation, assistive technology and sensory technology.
* Managing Microsoft 365 and other organisational software.
* Managing broadband, Wi-Fi and network infrastructure across our properties, working alongside our IT partners.
* Providing technical support to colleagues and the people we support.
* Working with suppliers and technical support teams to resolve issues and develop solutions.
* Maintaining accurate hardware and software inventories, user accounts and access arrangements.
* Supporting the security of our systems and helping ensure our data is managed appropriately and in line with current legislation.
* Providing some programming and technical support for the Style Acre website.
* Supporting technology-related projects and organisational development.
* Managing the disposal of redundant and outdated technology securely and responsibly.

### **Technology for Independence**

One of the most exciting parts of this role is managing our **Technology for Independence** project.

You’ll work with colleagues and our Senior Leadership Team to regularly review how technology can support the people we support, helping us make the most of developments in assistive, sensory and other technologies.

You’ll also support people working within the Style Acre IT department, helping them develop their skills and contribute meaningfully to our organisation.

### **Looking to the future**

Technology is changing rapidly, and we want Style Acre to embrace the opportunities it brings while doing so safely and responsibly.

You’ll help us explore and develop our use of **Artificial Intelligence**, ensuring we understand its benefits and risks and use it in ways that are appropriate, secure and beneficial to the organisation and the people we support.

We’ll also support you to keep your own knowledge and skills up to date through training, online learning, research and occasional industry events.

### **About you**

We’re looking for someone who is technically capable, curious and practical, with a genuine desire to use technology to solve problems and improve people's lives.

You’ll need to be comfortable working independently, managing a varied workload and explaining technical issues to people with different levels of IT experience. You’ll also need good organisational skills and an understanding of the importance of data security, confidentiality and compliance.

You don’t need to know everything – technology is constantly evolving. What matters is that you’re willing to learn, investigate problems, find solutions and keep developing your knowledge.

Most importantly, you’ll share Style Acre’s commitment to supporting people to live the lives they choose.

### **Why join Style Acre?**

At Style Acre, you’ll have the opportunity to do much more than keep our computers running.

You’ll help shape how a growing charity uses technology, while directly contributing to greater independence and better outcomes for the people we support.

You’ll be joining an organisation that is committed to investing in its people, providing the training, development and support you need to succeed in your role and fulfil your potential.

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*

**The role**

The Financial Times has an opening for a professional services correspondent to join the London Newsroom.

This is a new role designed to expand and elevate our coverage of the professional services sector as the world’s top corporate advisers respond to AI disruption, slower growth and intensifying scrutiny on their activities.

Professional services is a core part of the FT’s global corporate coverage and this reporter will be expected to break news on the big strategy and IT consultancies, particularly McKinsey, Boston Consulting Group, Bain and Accenture, as well as contributing to covering the advisory operations of the Big Four – Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC. 

Working closely with our other professional services reporters, in London and New York, the correspondent will chart how AI is reshaping the sector globally. The technology threatens to wipe out parts of consultants’ businesses and kill off their traditional hourly billing model. But executives argue that the upheaval also presents a massive opportunity for the sector as companies seek advice on how to overhaul their IT, workforces and strategies. 

There is scope to break stories about job cuts and changes to the sector’s staffing model as firms respond to sluggish demand and turn to AI to do tasks previously carried out by armies of junior consultants. The role will involve working with the FT’s global network to dig into how AI is disrupting IT consulting firms’ lucrative business implementing enterprise software products from the likes of SAP and Salesforce. 

The reporter must be able to deliver scoops and inside-the-room insight on the executives who run the big consultancies, their pay and C-suite power dynamics within the firms. The professional services sector has long been a source of regulatory and reputational scandals, while the incursion of private equity has fuelled the growth of challengers to the dominant players, offering great scope for original reporting that can attract readers to the FT. 

You will have to work closely with colleagues from across the newsroom, particularly the US Professional Services Editor and the London-based Accountancy Correspondent. You will also be expected to contribute across different media as the FT expands its professional services coverage. 

**Key responsibilities**

* Bring in high-profile scoops about the big professional services firms on issues such as: work won and lost, financial performance, strategic changes, adoption of AI and technology, behaviour and workplace culture, regulatory interventions, leadership changes and M&A.
* Deliver deeply reported analyses on the changing business models of professional services groups, their business relationships with AI, tech and software groups and their importance in wider society.
* Be the first to report on the roles of consultants in big corporate stories in other sectors, such as turnaround plans and strategic overhauls at blue-chip companies.
* Weekend shifts are required as part of the newsroom rota.
* Working with, and providing cover for, reporters on the professional services team during absences.

**Please submit your application by the end of the day, Monday 12th October 2026.**

**The use of AI**

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

**Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion**

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

**What’s in it for you? Our benefits**

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

**Accessibility**

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.
